-- WARNING: This schema is for context only and is not meant to be run.
-- Table order and constraints may not be valid for execution.

CREATE TABLE public.account_app_access (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid NOT NULL,
  app_id uuid NOT NULL,
  plan_id uuid,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'::text CHECK (status = ANY (ARRAY['active'::text, 'suspended'::text, 'cancelled'::text])),
  activated_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  expires_at timestamp with time zone,
  created_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT account_app_access_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT account_app_access_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT account_app_access_app_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (app_id) REFERENCES public.apps(id),
  CONSTRAINT account_app_access_plan_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (plan_id) REFERENCES public.plans(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.account_users (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid NOT NULL,
  user_id uuid NOT NULL,
  role USER-DEFINED NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member'::account_role,
  created_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT account_users_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT account_users_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT account_users_user_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES public.users(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.accounts (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name text NOT NULL,
  slug text UNIQUE,
  owner_user_id uuid NOT NULL,
  billing_email text,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'::text CHECK (status = ANY (ARRAY['active'::text, 'suspended'::text, 'deleted'::text])),
  created_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT accounts_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT accounts_owner_user_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (owner_user_id) REFERENCES public.users(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.activity_log (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  team_id uuid,
  account_id uuid,
  user_id uuid,
  action text,
  entity_type text,
  entity_id uuid,
  meta_json jsonb,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT activity_log_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT activity_log_team_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT activity_log_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT activity_log_user_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES public.users(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.agency_clients (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  team_id uuid,
  name text NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT agency_clients_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_clients_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_clients_team_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.agency_commissions (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  team_id uuid,
  placement_id uuid,
  amount numeric,
  status text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT agency_commissions_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_commissions_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_commissions_team_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_commissions_placement_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (placement_id) REFERENCES public.agency_placements(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.agency_communications (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  team_id uuid,
  client_id uuid,
  body text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT agency_communications_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_communications_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_communications_team_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_communications_client_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (client_id) REFERENCES public.agency_clients(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.agency_contacts (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  team_id uuid,
  client_id uuid,
  name text NOT NULL,
  email text,
  phone text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT agency_contacts_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_contacts_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_contacts_team_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_contacts_client_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (client_id) REFERENCES public.agency_clients(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.agency_invoices (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  team_id uuid,
  client_id uuid,
  amount numeric,
  status text,
  issued_at timestamp with time zone,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT agency_invoices_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_invoices_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_invoices_team_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_invoices_client_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (client_id) REFERENCES public.agency_clients(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.agency_mandates (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  team_id uuid,
  client_id uuid,
  title text NOT NULL,
  status text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT agency_mandates_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_mandates_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_mandates_team_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_mandates_client_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (client_id) REFERENCES public.agency_clients(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.agency_placements (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  team_id uuid,
  mandate_id uuid,
  status text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT agency_placements_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_placements_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_placements_team_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT agency_placements_mandate_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (mandate_id) REFERENCES public.agency_mandates(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.apps (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  slug text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name text NOT NULL,
  description text,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'::text CHECK (status = ANY (ARRAY['active'::text, 'disabled'::text, 'deprecated'::text])),
  created_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT apps_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.audit_logs (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  app_id uuid,
  user_id uuid,
  action text NOT NULL,
  entity_type text,
  entity_id uuid,
  changes_json jsonb,
  ip_address inet,
  user_agent text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT audit_logs_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT audit_logs_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT audit_logs_app_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (app_id) REFERENCES public.apps(id),
  CONSTRAINT audit_logs_user_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES public.users(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.auth_page_config (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  hero_headline text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Hire smarter. Rank better.'::text,
  hero_description text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'AI-powered recruitment that helps you find the best talent faster. Join 500+ companies already transforming their hiring.'::text,
  logo_url text,
  social_proof_count text NOT NULL DEFAULT '500+'::text,
  social_proof_label text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'hiring teams'::text,
  testimonials_json jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[{"name": "Sarah Chen", "role": "VP of People", "quote": "Rankora cut our time-to-hire by 40%. The AI ranking saves our team 15+ hours per week on resume screening.", "rating": 5, "company": "TechCorp", "avatar_initials": "SC"}]'::jsonb,
  trust_badges_json jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[{"icon": "lock", "label": "256-bit SSL"}, {"icon": "shield", "label": "SOC 2 Compliant"}, {"icon": "check-circle", "label": "GDPR Ready"}]'::jsonb,
  signup_benefits_json jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[{"text": "free trial with full access to all features", "highlight": "No credit card required"}, {"text": "screen 100 resumes in seconds, not hours", "highlight": "AI resume ranking"}, {"text": "invite your hiring team and start working together", "highlight": "Team collaboration"}, {"text": "no lock-in, no hidden fees, ever", "highlight": "Cancel anytime"}]'::jsonb,
  signup_headline text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Start hiring smarter in under 2 minutes'::text,
  signup_social_proof_count text NOT NULL DEFAULT '2,400+'::text,
  signup_social_proof_label text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'recruiters signed up this month'::text,
  google_auth_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  microsoft_auth_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  magic_link_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  signin_heading text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Welcome back'::text,
  signin_subheading text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Sign in to continue to your dashboard'::text,
  signup_heading text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Create your account'::text,
  signup_subheading text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Just your email to start'::text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT auth_page_config_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.availability_slots (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  team_id uuid,
  user_id uuid,
  start_time timestamp with time zone,
  end_time timestamp with time zone,
  is_booked boolean DEFAULT false,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT availability_slots_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT availability_slots_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT availability_slots_team_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT availability_slots_user_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES public.users(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.booking_tokens (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  token text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  resume_id uuid,
  job_id uuid,
  expires_at timestamp with time zone,
  used_at timestamp with time zone,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT booking_tokens_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT booking_tokens_resume_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (resume_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_resumes(id),
  CONSTRAINT booking_tokens_job_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (job_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_jobs(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.candidate_stages (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  resume_id uuid,
  job_id uuid,
  stage text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new'::text,
  moved_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  moved_by uuid,
  notes text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT candidate_stages_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT candidate_stages_resume_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (resume_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_resumes(id),
  CONSTRAINT candidate_stages_job_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (job_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_jobs(id),
  CONSTRAINT candidate_stages_moved_by_fkey FOREIGN KEY (moved_by) REFERENCES public.users(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.career_subscribers (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  career_page_id uuid,
  email text NOT NULL,
  created_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  team_id uuid,
  verified boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  CONSTRAINT career_subscribers_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT career_subscribers_career_page_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (career_page_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_career_pages(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.credit_packs (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name text NOT NULL,
  price numeric,
  price_cents integer,
  credits integer,
  active boolean DEFAULT true,
  is_trial boolean DEFAULT false,
  dodo_product_id text,
  dodo_credit_entitlement_id text,
  features jsonb,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT credit_packs_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.email_ingest_logs (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  user_id uuid,
  job_id uuid,
  sender text,
  subject text,
  status text,
  attachments_count integer DEFAULT 0,
  error_message text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT email_ingest_logs_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT email_ingest_logs_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT email_ingest_logs_user_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES public.users(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.email_templates (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  template_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  subject text NOT NULL,
  body_html text NOT NULL,
  body_text text,
  variables jsonb,
  is_active boolean DEFAULT true,
  updated_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT email_templates_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.guest_links (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  team_id uuid,
  job_id uuid,
  token text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  expires_at timestamp with time zone,
  created_by uuid,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT guest_links_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT guest_links_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT guest_links_team_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT guest_links_job_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (job_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_jobs(id),
  CONSTRAINT guest_links_created_by_fkey FOREIGN KEY (created_by) REFERENCES public.users(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.hire_outcomes (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  team_id uuid,
  resume_id uuid,
  job_id uuid,
  outcome text,
  hired_at timestamp with time zone,
  salary numeric,
  notes text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT hire_outcomes_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT hire_outcomes_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT hire_outcomes_team_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT hire_outcomes_resume_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (resume_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_resumes(id),
  CONSTRAINT hire_outcomes_job_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (job_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_jobs(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.integrations (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  key_name text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  display_name text,
  description text,
  is_configured boolean DEFAULT false,
  last_test_status text,
  last_tested_at timestamp with time zone,
  config_json jsonb,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT integrations_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.interviews (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  team_id uuid,
  job_id uuid,
  resume_id uuid,
  scheduled_at timestamp with time zone,
  duration_minutes integer,
  status text,
  notes text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT interviews_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT interviews_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT interviews_team_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT interviews_job_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (job_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_jobs(id),
  CONSTRAINT interviews_resume_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (resume_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_resumes(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.job_form_fields (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  job_id uuid,
  label text NOT NULL,
  field_type text NOT NULL,
  required boolean DEFAULT false,
  position integer DEFAULT 0,
  options jsonb,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT job_form_fields_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT job_form_fields_job_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (job_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_jobs(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.job_views (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  job_id uuid,
  viewer_ip inet,
  user_agent text,
  referer text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT job_views_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT job_views_job_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (job_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_jobs(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.notifications (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid,
  account_id uuid,
  type text,
  title text,
  body text,
  link text,
  read_at timestamp with time zone,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT notifications_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT notifications_user_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES public.users(id),
  CONSTRAINT notifications_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.outreach_history (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  team_id uuid,
  resume_id uuid,
  user_id uuid,
  channel text,
  status text,
  sent_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT outreach_history_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT outreach_history_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT outreach_history_team_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (team_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT outreach_history_resume_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (resume_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_resumes(id),
  CONSTRAINT outreach_history_user_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES public.users(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.outreach_log (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  enrollment_id uuid,
  step_id uuid,
  channel text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'email'::text,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'sent'::text,
  sent_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  opened_at timestamp with time zone,
  clicked_at timestamp with time zone,
  replied_at timestamp with time zone,
  error text,
  CONSTRAINT outreach_log_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT outreach_log_enrollment_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (enrollment_id) REFERENCES public.sequence_enrollments(id),
  CONSTRAINT outreach_log_step_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (step_id) REFERENCES public.sequence_steps(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.payments (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  account_id uuid,
  user_id uuid,
  plan_id uuid,
  amount numeric,
  amount_cents integer,
  currency text DEFAULT 'USD'::text,
  credits_purchased integer,
  status text,
  provider text,
  provider_payment_id text,
  dodo_payment_id text,
  dodo_checkout_session_id text,
  razorpay_payment_id text,
  razorpay_order_id text,
  pack_id uuid,
  plan_type text,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT payments_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT payments_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT payments_user_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES public.users(id),
  CONSTRAINT payments_plan_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (plan_id) REFERENCES public.plans(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.plans (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  app_id uuid NOT NULL,
  slug text NOT NULL,
  name text NOT NULL,
  description text,
  billing_type text NOT NULL CHECK (billing_type = ANY (ARRAY['free'::text, 'subscription'::text, 'one_time'::text])),
  price_cents integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (price_cents >= 0),
  currency text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USD'::text,
  interval text CHECK ("interval" = ANY (ARRAY['month'::text, 'year'::text, NULL::text])),
  limits_json jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'::text CHECK (status = ANY (ARRAY['active'::text, 'archived'::text])),
  created_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT plans_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT plans_app_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (app_id) REFERENCES public.apps(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.prompt_versions (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  prompt_type text NOT NULL,
  version integer NOT NULL,
  content text,
  model_name text,
  temperature numeric,
  is_active boolean DEFAULT false,
  created_by uuid,
  created_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT prompt_versions_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT prompt_versions_created_by_fkey FOREIGN KEY (created_by) REFERENCES public.users(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.ranking_config (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  system_prompt text,
  model_name text,
  temperature numeric DEFAULT 0.2,
  weights_json jsonb,
  updated_at timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT ranking_config_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.rankora_api_keys (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  app_id uuid NOT NULL,
  account_id uuid NOT NULL,
  created_by uuid,
  name text NOT NULL,
  key_prefix text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  key_hash text NOT NULL,
  last_used_at timestamp with time zone,
  expires_at timestamp with time zone,
  revoked_at timestamp with time zone,
  created_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT rankora_api_keys_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT rankora_api_keys_app_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (app_id) REFERENCES public.apps(id),
  CONSTRAINT rankora_api_keys_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT rankora_api_keys_created_by_fkey FOREIGN KEY (created_by) REFERENCES public.users(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.rankora_applications (
  id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  app_id uuid NOT NULL,
  account_id uuid NOT NULL,
  job_id uuid,
  candidate_name text NOT NULL,
  candidate_email text NOT NULL,
  candidate_phone text,
  resume_path text,
  custom_fields_json jsonb,
  source text,
  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'new'::text CHECK (status = ANY (ARRAY['new'::text, 'reviewed'::text, 'interviewed'::text, 'hired'::text, 'rejected'::text])),
  created_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamp with time zone NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT rankora_applications_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id),
  CONSTRAINT rankora_applications_app_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (app_id) REFERENCES public.apps(id),
  CONSTRAINT rankora_applications_account_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (account_id) REFERENCES public.accounts(id),
  CONSTRAINT rankora_applications_job_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (job_id) REFERENCES public.rankora_jobs(id)
);
CREATE TABLE public.rankora_candidate_notes (

The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

Check the target project for existing components, layout patterns,and tokens that match the design intent. Reuse what the project already has instead of generating new code from sc… [truncated]

## claude.ai Webflow
Call webflow_guide_tool once to learn available Webflow MCP capabilities before using any other tools. Only call it once per session.

## claude.ai Windsor.ai
This MCP server provides access to the Windsor.ai API, which allows
retrieving analytical data from various data sources such as Facebook, Google Ads, and
more using connectors.

When interacting with this MCP server, follow these steps:

1. Call the "get_connectors" tool to get all available connectors and their connected
   accounts.
2. If a connector the user wants is not yet connected, call
   "get_connector_authorization_url" to get a link they can open in their browser to
   set it up (works for all connector types, OAuth and manual).
3. Call the "get_options" tool to list all available fields, date filters and options
   for a specific connector and accounts.
4. Call the "get_fields" tool to get detailed information about specific fields
   of a given connector. This includes field descriptions, their types and the tables
   they belong to. Fields with "NUMERIC" or "PERCENT" types are metrics, while others
   are dimensions. Metrics will be aggregated depending on the dimensions selected.
5. Call the "get_data" tool to retrieve data from a specific connector by providing
   the connector ID, list of account IDs, list of field IDs, date filter, date range,
   and any options and filters if needed.

content.text:
Based on my comprehensive exploration of the Rankora codebase, here's the detailed report on the multi-app/multi-tenant architecture:

## Rankora Multi-App/Multi-Tenant Architecture Report

### 1. How `app_id` is Used Across the Codebase

**Database Schema (Primary Location):**
- **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/migrations/20260420000001_bubs_core.sql`
  - Lines 51-60: `apps` table definition
  - Lines 338-349: `get_app_id()` function that resolves app slug to UUID
  
**Key Rankora Tables with `app_id` Foreign Key:**
- **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/migrations/20260420000002_bubs_rankora_tables.sql`
  - Line 27: `rankora_jobs` table has `app_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES apps(id)`
  - Line 57: `rankora_resumes` table has `app_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES apps(id)`
  - Line 88: `rankora_results` table has `app_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES apps(id)`
  - Lines 43, 78, 116: Composite indexes on `(account_id, app_id)` for efficient multi-tenant queries
  
**Other Tables with app_id Foreign Keys:**
- `rankora_applications` (line 127)
- `rankora_candidate_notes` (line 224)
- `rankora_candidate_tags` (line 246)
- `rankora_tasks`, `rankora_pipeline_stages`, `rankora_feature_flags`, `rankora_changelog`, etc.

### 2. Apps Table Structure and Registration Flow

**Apps Table Definition:**
- **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/migrations/20260420000001_bubs_core.sql` (Lines 51-60)
- Columns:
  - `id` (uuid PRIMARY KEY, auto-generated)
  - `slug` (text UNIQUE NOT NULL) - e.g., 'rankora'
  - `name` (text NOT NULL) - display name
  - `description` (text)
  - `status` (text DEFAULT 'active', CHECK: 'active', 'disabled', 'deprecated')
  - `created_at`, `updated_at` (timestamptz)

**Multi-App Entitlement Junction Table:**
- **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/migrations/20260420000001_bubs_core.sql` (Lines 180-201)
- Table: `account_app_access`
  - `account_id` (uuid) + `app_id` (uuid) - UNIQUE pair
  - `plan_id` (uuid) - which plan/tier the account is on for this app
  - `status` ('active', 'suspended', 'cancelled')
  - `activated_at`, `expires_at` - subscription dates
  - Comment: "Entitlement table. Determines which accounts can use which apps and on what plan."

**App Registration Flow:**
- **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/migrations/20260420000007_bubs_bootstrap_and_seed.sql`
  - Lines 95-108: When a user signs up, the bootstrap process:
    1. Creates/finds the user's personal `account` (Lines 79-87)
    2. Adds them as `owner` in `account_users` (Lines 91-93)
    3. **Inserts into `account_app_access`** (Lines 98-108):
       - Links account → app ('rankora')
       - Assigns either 'pro' or 'free' plan based on email
       - Sets status to 'active'

### 3. Rankora App ID Constant/Config

**How to Get App ID at Runtime:**
- **Function:** `get_app_id('rankora')` - SQL function
  - **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/migrations/20260420000001_bubs_core.sql` (Lines 291-299)
  - SQL: `SELECT id FROM apps WHERE slug = 'rankora' AND status = 'active' LIMIT 1;`
  - Used throughout RLS policies and edge functions as: `get_app_id('rankora')`

**No Client-Side Constant:** The codebase does NOT expose a hardcoded `RANKORA_APP_ID` constant in the frontend code. Instead:
- The UUID is resolved dynamically via `get_app_id('rankora')` in SQL/RLS policies
- Clients don't need to know the UUID — they work through account_app_access entitlements

**Usage Pattern in Bootstrap:**
- **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/migrations/20260420000007_bubs_bootstrap_and_seed.sql`
  - Line 44: `v_rankora_id := get_app_id('rankora');`
  - Then used in INSERT/SELECT queries for seeding data

### 4. Query Filtering: `app_id` vs `account_id`

**Pattern: Dual-Key Filtering**

All Rankora tables use composite keys `(account_id, app_id)` for:
1. **Multi-tenancy isolation** - account_id isolates data per customer
2. **App scoping** - app_id locks data to the Rankora app only

**RLS Policies (Enforcement at Database Level):**
- **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/migrations/20260420000002_bubs_rankora_tables.sql`

**SELECT Policies (Lines 431-432, 451-452, 469-470, etc.):**
```sql
CREATE POLICY rankora_jobs_select ON rankora_jobs FOR SELECT
  USING (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id));
```
- Must be member of the account AND have active entitlement for the app

**INSERT Policies (Lines 434-440, 454-459, etc.):**
```sql
CREATE POLICY rankora_jobs_insert ON rankora_jobs FOR INSERT
  WITH CHECK (
    is_account_member(account_id)
    AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id)
    AND app_id = get_app_id('rankora')  -- HARD CONSTRAINT
    AND created_by = auth.uid()
  );
```
- Explicitly enforces `app_id = get_app_id('rankora')` — cannot insert into wrong app

**Key Helper Functions:**
- **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/supabase/migrations/20260420000001_bubs_core.sql`
  - `has_app_access(account_id, app_id)` (Lines 338-349): Checks `account_app_access` table for active entitlement
  - `is_account_member(account_id)` (Lines 310-319): Checks `account_users` table
  - `is_account_admin(account_id)` (implicit): Admin role in account_users

**Client-Side Query Patterns:**
- **File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/hooks/usePipelineStages.tsx` (Lines 46-52)
  ```typescript
  const { data, error } = await (supabase as any)
    .from("pipeline_stages")
    .select("*")
    .eq("team_id", teamId)  // Note: this codebase still uses legacy "team_id"
  ```
  - Modern hooks filter by `team_id` (legacy) — RLS policies enforce app_id server-side
  - Clients don't explicitly pass app_id in queries; RLS enforces it via `get_app_id('rankora')`

### 5. Architecture Summary

| Component | Location | Purpose |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| **Apps Registry** | 20260420000001_bubs_core.sql:51-60 | Central registry of Boldteq SaaS apps |
| **App Access Control** | 20260420000001_bubs_core.sql:180-201 | `account_app_access` junction table for entitlements |
| **App ID Resolution** | 20260420000001_bubs_core.sql:291-299 | `get_app_id('rankora')` SQL function |
| **RLS Policies** | 20260420000002_bubs_rankora_tables.sql:430-575 | Enforce both `account_id` AND `app_id` in all table policies |
| **Bootstrap/Seeding** | 20260420000007_bubs_bootstrap_and_seed.sql:34-112 | Auto-grants Rankora access to new users via `account_app_access` |
| **Composite Indexes** | 20260420000002_bubs_rankora_tables.sql:43,78,116 | `(account_id, app_id)` indexes for query performance |

**Key Insight:** Rankora is built on Boldteq's **multi-app BUBS (Boldteq Unified Backend System)** architecture. The platform can host multiple SaaS products; Rankora is just one app in the registry. All data isolation is enforced at the database level via RLS policies checking both account membership AND app entitlement.

# Plan: Add `app_id` to All Legacy Tables + Fix RLS Policies

## Context

Rankora's database has two generations of tables:
- **BUBS-era (`rankora_*`)**: 20 tables with `app_id` FK + RLS enforcing `has_app_access(account_id, app_id)`
- **Legacy (non-prefixed)**: 34 tables missing `app_id` — no app-level isolation, many have wide-open `true` RLS policies

This migration adds `app_id` to all 34 legacy tables, backfills existing rows, and replaces the weak RLS policies with proper `is_account_member() AND has_app_access()` checks matching the `rankora_*` pattern.

## Single Migration File

**File:** `supabase/migrations/2026XXXXXXXXXX_add_app_id_to_legacy_tables.sql`

### Part 1: Add `app_id` column to all 34 tables

For each table, the pattern is:
```sql
ALTER TABLE <table> ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS app_id uuid REFERENCES apps(id);
UPDATE <table> SET app_id = get_app_id('rankora') WHERE app_id IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE <table> ALTER COLUMN app_id SET NOT NULL;
```

**Category 1 — 23 tables with `account_id` (need `app_id` + composite index):**
1. `activity_log`
2. `agency_clients`
3. `agency_commissions`
4. `agency_communications`
5. `agency_contacts`
6. `agency_invoices`
7. `agency_mandates`
8. `agency_placements`
9. `availability_slots`
10. `guest_links`
11. `hire_outcomes`
12. `interviews`
13. `notifications`
14. `outreach_history`
15. `payments`
16. `scorecard_responses`
17. `scorecard_templates`
18. `sequences`
19. `stage_tracker`
20. `talent_pool`
21. `talent_pool_members`
22. `team_invitations`
23. `webhook_configs`

Each gets: `CREATE INDEX idx_<table>_account_app ON <table>(account_id, app_id);`

**Category 2 — 11 tables connected via FK chain (need `app_id` + single index):**
1. `booking_tokens`
2. `candidate_stages`
3. `career_subscribers`
4. `job_form_fields`
5. `job_views`
6. `outreach_log`
7. `sequence_enrollments`
8. `sequence_steps`
9. `stage_automations`
10. `stage_history`
11. `sms_logs`

Each gets: `CREATE INDEX idx_<table>_app ON <table>(app_id);`

### Part 2: Drop all existing RLS policies on these tables, then create proper ones

**Current state of RLS (problematic):**
- Many tables have 2-3 overlapping policies from migrations 0006, 0013, 0015
- 14+ tables have `USING (true)` SELECT — any authenticated user can read all rows
- Write policies only check `auth.uid() IS NOT NULL` — any user can write to any row

**New RLS pattern per table (matching `rankora_*` convention):**

For tables with `account_id`:
```sql
-- SELECT: must be account member with app access
CREATE POLICY <table>_select ON <table> FOR SELECT
  USING (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id));

-- INSERT: must be account member with app access, app must be rankora
CREATE POLICY <table>_insert ON <table> FOR INSERT
  WITH CHECK (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id)
              AND app_id = get_app_id('rankora'));

-- UPDATE: same as select
CREATE POLICY <table>_update ON <table> FOR UPDATE
  USING (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id));

-- DELETE: same as select
CREATE POLICY <table>_delete ON <table> FOR DELETE
  USING (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id));
```

**Special cases:**
- `notifications` — keep `user_id = auth.uid()` as primary check (user-scoped), add `app_id` check
- `sms_logs` — keep `user_id = auth.uid()` as primary check, add `app_id` check
- `payments` — keep `user_id = auth.uid() OR is_account_member(account_id)`, add `app_id` check
- `booking_tokens`, `job_views`, `career_subscribers` — SELECT stays public (no auth required for public-facing pages), but INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE require account membership + app access
- `job_form_fields`, `stage_automations` — SELECT public for application forms, writes require membership
- `talent_pool_members` — needs JOIN-based check through `talent_pool.account_id`

### Part 3: Composite indexes

Add `(account_id, app_id)` composite indexes to all Category 1 tables and `(app_id)` indexes to Category 2 tables for RLS performance.

## Files to Modify

1. **New file:** `supabase/migrations/20260413000001_add_app_id_to_legacy_tables.sql` — the full migration
2. **No frontend changes needed** — RLS enforces app_id server-side; client queries already filter by account_id and RLS adds the app_id check transparently

## Verification

1. Apply migration: `supabase db push` (or `supabase db reset` on develop)
2. Verify all 34 tables have `app_id` column: `SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE column_name = 'app_id'`
3. Verify no table has `USING (true)` policies left: check `pg_policies` view
4. Test existing features in dev:
   - Dashboard loads (activity_log, notifications)
   - Tasks page works (rankora_tasks already had app_id)
   - Team/invitations work (team_invitations)
   - Talent pool page works
   - Sequences page works
   - Payments/billing display correctly
5. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` — should pass (no frontend type changes)
6. Run `npx vitest run` — should pass

# Plan: Add `app_id` to Legacy Tables Missing App Scope

## Context

Rankora's database has two generations of tables:
- **BUBS-era (`rankora_*`)**: 20 tables with proper `app_id` FK + RLS policies enforcing `has_app_access(account_id, app_id)`
- **Legacy (non-prefixed)**: 35 tables created before the multi-app architecture. These lack `app_id`, meaning they can't enforce app-level isolation via RLS.

If Boldteq adds a second app to the platform, all legacy table data would be visible across apps. Even today, RLS policies on these tables are weaker (no `has_app_access()` check).

## Tables Requiring `app_id` Addition (23 tables — Category 1)

These store app-scoped business data and need a direct `app_id NOT NULL REFERENCES apps(id)`:

1. `activity_log`
2. `agency_clients`
3. `agency_commissions`
4. `agency_communications`
5. `agency_contacts`
6. `agency_invoices`
7. `agency_mandates`
8. `agency_placements`
9. `availability_slots`
10. `guest_links`
11. `hire_outcomes`
12. `interviews`
13. `notifications`
14. `outreach_history`
15. `payments`
16. `scorecard_responses`
17. `scorecard_templates`
18. `sequences`
19. `stage_tracker`
20. `talent_pool`
21. `talent_pool_members`
22. `team_invitations`
23. `webhook_configs`

## Tables Needing `app_id` for Direct RLS (11 tables — Category 2)

These connect to `rankora_*` tables via FK but lack their own `app_id` for standalone RLS:

1. `booking_tokens`
2. `candidate_stages`
3. `career_subscribers`
4. `job_form_fields`
5. `job_views`
6. `outreach_log`
7. `sequence_enrollments`
8. `sequence_steps`
9. `stage_automations`
10. `stage_history`
11. `sms_logs`

## Tables That Are Fine Without `app_id` (legitimately global)

- `apps`, `accounts`, `account_users`, `users` — cross-app entities
- `credit_packs`, `email_templates`, `integrations` — global config/catalog
- `ranking_config`, `prompt_versions` — global AI config
- `seo_pages`, `seo_settings` — site-level
- `subscription_webhooks`, `system_error_logs` — global audit
- `rankora_platform_config` — keyed by `account_id`, app-specific by naming convention

## Migration Approach

### Step 1: Create a new Supabase migration file
File: `supabase/migrations/2026XXXXXXXXXX_add_app_id_to_legacy_tables.sql`

For each table:
```sql
-- 1. Add nullable column
ALTER TABLE <table> ADD COLUMN app_id uuid REFERENCES apps(id);

-- 2. Backfill existing rows with Rankora's app_id
UPDATE <table> SET app_id = get_app_id('rankora') WHERE app_id IS NULL;

-- 3. Make NOT NULL
ALTER TABLE <table> ALTER COLUMN app_id SET NOT NULL;

-- 4. Add composite index
CREATE INDEX idx_<table>_account_app ON <table>(account_id, app_id);
```

### Step 2: Update RLS policies on each table
Add `has_app_access(account_id, app_id)` check to SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies.

### Step 3: Update frontend queries
Any hooks/components querying these tables may need to include `app_id` in filters (though RLS handles enforcement server-side).

## Files to Modify
- New migration: `supabase/migrations/2026XXXXXXXXXX_add_app_id_to_legacy_tables.sql`
- Potentially update RLS policies in existing migration or new migration
- Frontend hooks that query legacy tables (find via grep for table names)

## Verification
1. `supabase db push` — migration applies cleanly
2. Check all 34 tables now have `app_id` column
3. Verify RLS policies include `has_app_access()` on all app-scoped tables
4. Test existing features (tasks, activity, team, agency, talent pool pages) still work

- `notifications` — keep `user_id = auth.uid()` as primary check (user-scoped), add `app_id` check
- `sms_logs` — keep `user_id = auth.uid()` as primary check, add `app_id` check
- `payments` — keep `user_id = auth.uid() OR is_account_member(account_id)`, add `app_id` check
- `booking_tokens`, `job_views`, `career_subscribers` — SELECT stays public (no auth required for public-facing pages), but INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE require account membership + app access
- `job_form_fields`, `stage_automations` — SELECT public for application forms, writes require membership
- `talent_pool_members` — needs JOIN-based check through `talent_pool.account_id`

### Part 3: Composite indexes

Add `(account_id, app_id)` composite indexes to all Category 1 tables and `(app_id)` indexes to Category 2 tables for RLS performance.

**What it does:**
1. **Adds `app_id`** (NOT NULL, FK to `apps`) to all 34 legacy tables, backfilled with `get_app_id('rankora')`

4. **Adds composite indexes** — `(account_id, app_id)` for Category 1, `(app_id)` for Category 2

**Special cases handled:**
- `notifications`, `sms_logs`, `availability_slots` — user-scoped (`user_id = auth.uid()`)
- `payments` — user OR account member scoped
- `guest_links`, `booking_tokens`, `job_form_fields`, `job_views`, `career_subscribers` — public SELECT preserved for anon access
- `team_invitations` — INSERT requires `is_account_admin()`
- `talent_pool_members` — JOIN-based check through `talent_pool.account_id`

content.text:
Perfect! Now I have all the information I need. Let me compile my findings:

## Analysis Summary: app_id Handling on Frontend Inserts

Based on my investigation of the Rankora codebase, here's a **critical finding** regarding how app_id is handled when the frontend inserts data:

### 1. **MIGRATION 20260420000005 - Compat Views (jobs, resumes, results)**

The `jobs` and `resumes` views have **INSTEAD OF INSERT triggers** that automatically populate app_id:

**jobs_insert_trigger() (line 142-171):**
```sql
INSERT INTO rankora_jobs (
  id, app_id, account_id, created_by, ...
) VALUES (
  ...,
  get_app_id('rankora'),  <-- AUTO-POPULATED
  ...
)
```

**resumes_insert_trigger() (line 247-286):**
```sql
INSERT INTO rankora_resumes (
  id, app_id, account_id, job_id, created_by, ...
) VALUES (
  ...,
  get_app_id('rankora'),  <-- AUTO-POPULATED
  ...
)
```

**Status:** Jobs and resumes views are safe - app_id is auto-filled via trigger.

---

### 2. **MIGRATION 20260420000002 - rankora_* Tables**

- **rankora_jobs.app_id**: `NOT NULL` with **NO DEFAULT** (line 27)
- **rankora_resumes.app_id**: `NOT NULL` with **NO DEFAULT** (line 57)
- **rankora_results.app_id**: `NOT NULL` with **NO DEFAULT** (line 88)
- **rankora_tasks.app_id**: `NOT NULL` with **NO DEFAULT** (line 191)

All rankora_* tables have app_id NOT NULL without a DEFAULT value, but this is **protected** by the INSTEAD OF INSERT triggers in the compat views.

---

### 3. **MIGRATION 20260420000017 - Legacy Tables**

**Critical Finding:** App_id was added to 34 legacy tables (activity_log, notifications, availability_slots, sequences, talent_pool, interviews, guest_links, team_invitations, payments, etc.) with:

```sql
ALTER TABLE [table] ADD COLUMN app_id uuid REFERENCES apps(id);
UPDATE [table] SET app_id = $1 WHERE app_id IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE [table] ALTER COLUMN app_id SET NOT NULL;
```

**app_id is NOW NOT NULL on these 34 tables WITH NO DEFAULT VALUE AND NO BEFORE/INSTEAD OF TRIGGERS.**

---

### 4. **Frontend Code - NOT Passing app_id**

I examined multiple INSERT calls in src/:

- `/src/components/candidate/ContactStrip.tsx` (line 28): `outreach_log` insert - **NO app_id passed**
- `/src/components/GuestLinkDialog.tsx` (line 89): `guest_links` insert - **NO app_id passed**
- `/src/hooks/useSequences.ts` (line 211): `sequences` insert - **NO app_id passed**
- `/src/hooks/useAgencyClients.ts` (line 68): `agency_clients` insert - **NO app_id passed**

All INSERT calls I found pass `team_id` (as account_id) and `user_id`, but **NONE pass app_id**.

---

### 5. **RLS Policies on Legacy Tables**

The new RLS policies in migration 17 check `app_id = get_app_id('rankora')` on INSERT (e.g., lines 395-399), but RLS only prevents unauthorized access - it doesn't auto-populate the column.

---

## CRITICAL ISSUE

**The frontend will fail on INSERT to legacy tables** because:

1. All 34 legacy tables now have `app_id NOT NULL`
2. `app_id` has **NO DEFAULT VALUE**
3. `app_id` has **NO BEFORE INSERT trigger** to auto-populate it
4. Frontend code **DOES NOT PASS app_id** in any INSERT payload

**Example failure:**
```javascript
supabase.from("sequences").insert({ ...input, user_id: user.id })
// Will fail with: null value in column "app_id" violates not-null constraint
```

---

## Recommended Fix

Add BEFORE INSERT triggers to all 34 legacy tables to auto-populate app_id:

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION set_legacy_app_id()
RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  NEW.app_id := get_app_id('rankora');
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

-- Apply to all 34 tables
CREATE TRIGGER activity_log_set_app_id BEFORE INSERT ON activity_log
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_legacy_app_id();
-- ... repeat for all 34 tables
```

This matches the pattern already established in the compat views (jobs, resumes, results).

Perfect! Now I have all the information I need. Let me compile my findings:

## Analysis Summary: app_id Handling on Frontend Inserts

Based on my investigation of the Rankora codebase, here's a **critical finding** regarding how app_id is handled when the frontend inserts data:

### 1. **MIGRATION 20260420000005 - Compat Views (jobs, resumes, results)**

The `jobs` and `resumes` views have **INSTEAD OF INSERT triggers** that automatically populate app_id:

**jobs_insert_trigger() (line 142-171):**
```sql
INSERT INTO rankora_jobs (
  id, app_id, account_id, created_by, ...
) VALUES (
  ...,
  get_app_id('rankora'),  <-- AUTO-POPULATED
  ...
)
```

**resumes_insert_trigger() (line 247-286):**
```sql
INSERT INTO rankora_resumes (
  id, app_id, account_id, job_id, created_by, ...
) VALUES (
  ...,
  get_app_id('rankora'),  <-- AUTO-POPULATED
  ...
)
```

**Status:** Jobs and resumes views are safe - app_id is auto-filled via trigger.

---

### 2. **MIGRATION 20260420000002 - rankora_* Tables**

- **rankora_jobs.app_id**: `NOT NULL` with **NO DEFAULT** (line 27)
- **rankora_resumes.app_id**: `NOT NULL` with **NO DEFAULT** (line 57)
- **rankora_results.app_id**: `NOT NULL` with **NO DEFAULT** (line 88)
- **rankora_tasks.app_id**: `NOT NULL` with **NO DEFAULT** (line 191)

All rankora_* tables have app_id NOT NULL without a DEFAULT value, but this is **protected** by the INSTEAD OF INSERT triggers in the compat views.

---

### 3. **MIGRATION 20260420000017 - Legacy Tables**

**Critical Finding:** App_id was added to 34 legacy tables (activity_log, notifications, availability_slots, sequences, talent_pool, interviews, guest_links, team_invitations, payments, etc.) with:

```sql
ALTER TABLE [table] ADD COLUMN app_id uuid REFERENCES apps(id);
UPDATE [table] SET app_id = $1 WHERE app_id IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE [table] ALTER COLUMN app_id SET NOT NULL;
```

**app_id is NOW NOT NULL on these 34 tables WITH NO DEFAULT VALUE AND NO BEFORE/INSTEAD OF TRIGGERS.**

---

### 4. **Frontend Code - NOT Passing app_id**

I examined multiple INSERT calls in src/:

- `/src/components/candidate/ContactStrip.tsx` (line 28): `outreach_log` insert - **NO app_id passed**
- `/src/components/GuestLinkDialog.tsx` (line 89): `guest_links` insert - **NO app_id passed**
- `/src/hooks/useSequences.ts` (line 211): `sequences` insert - **NO app_id passed**
- `/src/hooks/useAgencyClients.ts` (line 68): `agency_clients` insert - **NO app_id passed**

All INSERT calls I found pass `team_id` (as account_id) and `user_id`, but **NONE pass app_id**.

---

### 5. **RLS Policies on Legacy Tables**

The new RLS policies in migration 17 check `app_id = get_app_id('rankora')` on INSERT (e.g., lines 395-399), but RLS only prevents unauthorized access - it doesn't auto-populate the column.

---

## CRITICAL ISSUE

**The frontend will fail on INSERT to legacy tables** because:

1. All 34 legacy tables now have `app_id NOT NULL`
2. `app_id` has **NO DEFAULT VALUE**
3. `app_id` has **NO BEFORE INSERT trigger** to auto-populate it
4. Frontend code **DOES NOT PASS app_id** in any INSERT payload

**Example failure:**
```javascript
supabase.from("sequences").insert({ ...input, user_id: user.id })
// Will fail with: null value in column "app_id" violates not-null constraint
```

---

## Recommended Fix

Add BEFORE INSERT triggers to all 34 legacy tables to auto-populate app_id:

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION set_legacy_app_id()
RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  NEW.app_id := get_app_id('rankora');
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

-- Apply to all 34 tables
CREATE TRIGGER activity_log_set_app_id BEFORE INSERT ON activity_log
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_legacy_app_id();
-- ... repeat for all 34 tables
```

This matches the pattern already established in the compat views (jobs, resumes, results).
Critical bug confirmed — all 34 tables will fail on INSERT because `app_id` is `NOT NULL` with no DEFAULT and no trigger, and the frontend never passes it. Let me fix this now.

Based on my thorough analysis of the Rankora codebase, I've identified **8 critical bugs** across multiple pages. Here's the detailed report:

---

### **1. CRITICAL: CareerSettings.tsx - Missing team_id/account_id on INSERT**
**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/legacy-pages/CareerSettings.tsx`  
**Lines:** 526-528  
**Issue:** When creating a new `career_page_config` record, the `INSERT` is missing both `team_id` and `account_id` columns. The schema requires `account_id` (NOT NULL), but the payload only includes display fields.

**Current Code:**
```typescript
const { data: inserted, error } = await (supabase as any)
  .from("career_page_config")
  .insert(payload)  // payload has no team_id or account_id
```

**Database Expectation:** `career_page_config` table requires `account_id` (from schema migration 20260420000002_bubs_rankora_tables.sql, line 155)

**Fix Needed:** Add `team_id` and `account_id` to the payload before insert:

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user (Yash Baldha, Founder of Boldteq) is working on Rankora — an AI resume ranking SaaS app built on Next.js 16 + Supabase (legacy Lovable/Stack A-Lovable stack, grandfathered). The requests in this conversation were:
   - **Initial:** "for all database can you please check for detect issue why in rankora all database not connected with app class and tag detect" — audit why tables weren't connected to the `apps` table (BUBS multi-app architecture)
   - **Approved Plan:** Full migration adding `app_id` to all 34 legacy tables with proper RLS
   - **Fix gaps:** "yes lets fix all bugs here and hardly change anything you want to make all same as before fully working. like on lovable all was working" — fix the 2 remaining gap tables AND ensure inserts still work (not breaking app)
   - **Current (pending):** "can you make sure in whole app no single bug for save failed currently i see lots of thing failing in app and not properly connected with database i think lets deep check and dont message me untill you fix all i want it to do whole app with properly functional and structured and proper thing and fully dynamic" — comprehensive deep fix of ALL app bugs, do not message until everything is fixed

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **BUBS Architecture** — Boldteq Unified Backend System: multi-app platform where each app is registered in the `apps` table; data isolated via `app_id` FK + `has_app_access(account_id, app_id)` RLS helper
   - **Multi-tenancy:** `account_id` for workspace isolation + `app_id` for app isolation, both enforced at RLS level
   - **Compat Views:** Frontend queries legacy-named views (`jobs`, `resumes`, `tasks`, `pipeline_stages`, etc.) that alias columns from `rankora_*` prefixed base tables
   - **INSTEAD OF Triggers:** PostgreSQL mechanism for making views writable; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on view is intercepted by trigger function which translates to base table operation
   - **RLS (Row Level Security):** Supabase/PostgreSQL feature; policies use helper functions `is_account_member(account_id)`, `has_app_access(account_id, app_id)`, `get_app_id('rankora')`
   - **`get_app_id('rankora')`:** SQL function returning UUID of Rankora from `apps` table; used as DEFAULT for `app_id` columns and in RLS WITH CHECK clauses
   - **`set_rankora_app_id()`:** BEFORE INSERT trigger function created in migration 0018 that auto-populates `app_id` if NULL
   - **Supabase migration sequencing:** Migrations run in filename order; later migrations override earlier ones (0014 beats 0011 beats 0005)
   - **`security_invoker = true`:** View setting that runs RLS as the querying user (not view owner); final state per migration 0014
   - **TanStack Query:** Used for all server state; `useQuery`/`useMutation` pattern throughout hooks
   - **`supabase as any` cast:** Used throughout frontend because many legacy table/view names are not in auto-generated types

3. Files and Code Sections:

   **Migration Files Created/Modified:**

   - `supabase/migrations/20260420000017_add_app_id_to_legacy_tables.sql` (CREATED)
     - Adds `app_id` column (NOT NULL, FK to `apps`) to 34 legacy tables
     - Backfills existing rows with `get_app_id('rankora')`
     - Drops all old weak RLS policies
     - Creates proper RLS policies with `is_account_member() AND has_app_access()`
     - Adds composite indexes `(account_id, app_id)`
     - Special cases: `booking_tokens` (no user_id on remote), `interviews`/`hire_outcomes`/`scorecard_responses`/`guest_links` all have `account_id` on remote

   - `supabase/migrations/20260420000018_fix_app_id_defaults_and_triggers.sql` (CREATED)
     - Creates shared trigger function `set_rankora_app_id()` — sets `app_id = get_app_id('rankora')` if NULL on INSERT
     - Adds `DEFAULT get_app_id('rankora')` to `app_id` on all 34 legacy tables
     - Adds BEFORE INSERT trigger on all 34 legacy tables
     - Adds `app_id` + DEFAULT + trigger to 2 remaining gaps: `rankora_platform_config` and `email_ingest_logs`
     - Adds DEFAULT + trigger as safety net on all 13 `rankora_*` base tables
     - Adds RLS policies for `email_ingest_logs`

   **Key existing migrations reviewed:**
   - `supabase/migrations/20260420000005_bubs_compat_views.sql` — defines `jobs`, `resumes`, `results`, `teams`, `team_members`, `platform_config` views; `teams` and `team_members` have NO triggers; `results` missing DELETE trigger
   - `supabase/migrations/20260420000006_bubs_admin_compat.sql` — defines `tasks`, `candidate_notes`, `candidate_tags`, `career_page_config`, `feature_requests`, `feature_request_votes`, `job_pipeline_stages`, `applications`, `api_keys` views — ALL missing INSTEAD OF triggers
   - `supabase/migrations/20260420000011_fix_database_connectivity.sql` — rebuilds `platform_config` view WITHOUT the `WHERE account_id = get_primary_account(auth.uid())` filter → bug: returns ALL accounts' config
   - `supabase/migrations/20260420000014_fix_security_definer_views.sql` — final state of views with `security_invoker = true`, also drops/recreates `platform_config` WITHOUT WHERE filter

   **Frontend hooks read:**

   - `src/hooks/useTasks.tsx` (read in full)
     - Queries `tasks` view with `.eq("team_id", teamId)` — correct
     - INSERT passes `team_id`, `created_by`, `related_entity_type`, `related_entity_id` — but `tasks` view has no INSERT trigger → FAILS
     - UPDATE/DELETE on `tasks` view — no trigger → FAILS
     ```typescript
     const { error } = await (supabase as any).from("tasks").insert({
       team_id: teamId,
       created_by: user?.id,
       related_entity_type: job_id ? "job" : candidate_id ? "candidate" : null,
       related_entity_id: job_id ?? candidate_id ?? null,
       ...rest,
     });
     ```

   - `src/hooks/useCandidateNotes.tsx` (read in full)
     - Filters by `job_id` — column does NOT exist in `rankora_candidate_notes`
     - INSERT passes: `resume_id`, `job_id` (WRONG), `author_id` (should be `created_by`), `note_type` (WRONG), `content` (should be `body`), `mentions` (WRONG)
     - No trigger on `candidate_notes` view → ALL operations fail
     ```typescript
     .insert({ resume_id: resumeId, job_id: jobId, author_id: user?.id, note_type: noteType, content, mentions: mentions ?? [] });
     ```

   - `src/hooks/useCandidateTags.tsx` (read in full)
     - Filters by `job_id` — does NOT exist in `rankora_candidate_tags`
     - INSERT passes `job_id` — WRONG column
     - Real-time subscription filters on `job_id` — wrong
     - No trigger on `candidate_tags` view → FAILS
     ```typescript
     .eq("job_id", jobId)  // WRONG — table has no job_id
     .insert({ resume_id: resumeId, job_id: jobId, tag, color, created_by: user.id }) // job_id WRONG
     ```

   - `src/hooks/usePipelineStages.tsx` (read in full)
     - Queries `pipeline_stages` view (which is a view of `job_pipeline_stages` view, which is view of `rankora_pipeline_stages`)
     - Queries filter by `team_id` — view exposes `account_id AS team_id` — correct mapping
     - INSERT: `.insert({ team_id: teamId, name, color, sort_order })` — view has NO trigger → FAILS
     - UPDATE/DELETE also fail — no triggers
     - `sort_order` passed but table has `position` column (view exposes `position` not `sort_order`)

   - `src/legacy-pages/Team.tsx` (partial, lines 240-320)
     - `handleChangeRole`: UPDATE on `team_members` view — no trigger → FAILS
     - `handleRemoveMember`: DELETE from `team_members` view — no trigger → FAILS
     - `handleLeaveTeam`: DELETE from `team_members` view — no trigger → FAILS
     - `handleSaveTeamName`: UPDATE on `teams` view — no trigger → FAILS

   - `src/legacy-pages/RequestFeature.tsx` (partial, lines 95-165)
     - INSERT into `feature_requests` view with `user_id` field — view exposes `created_by AS user_id` — no trigger → FAILS
     - SELECT from `feature_request_votes` — works (read)
     - Vote INSERT into `feature_request_votes` — no trigger → FAILS

   **View definitions (from migration 0006) — all missing triggers:**
   ```sql
   -- tasks view: assignee_user_id AS assigned_to
   SELECT id, account_id AS user_id, account_id AS team_id, account_id,
          created_by, assignee_user_id AS assigned_to, title, description,
          due_date, status, priority, related_entity_type, related_entity_id,
          completed_at, created_at, updated_at FROM rankora_tasks;

   -- candidate_notes view: body AS content (AND body)
   SELECT id, account_id AS user_id, account_id AS team_id, account_id,
          resume_id, created_by, body AS content, body, created_at, updated_at
   FROM rankora_candidate_notes;

   -- candidate_tags view: no job_id
   SELECT id, account_id AS user_id, account_id AS team_id, account_id,
          resume_id, created_by, tag, color, created_at
   FROM rankora_candidate_tags;

   -- pipeline_stages / job_pipeline_stages: position not sort_order
   SELECT id, account_id AS team_id, account_id, name, slug, color,
          position, is_default, created_at, updated_at
   FROM rankora_pipeline_stages;
   ```

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Migration 0017 first push attempt:** "Remote database is up to date" but columns not added — the migration was registered in history (from a prior db reset) but never executed. Fixed by running `supabase migration repair 20260420000017 --status reverted` then re-pushing.
   - **Migration 0017 second push attempt:** `ERROR: column "user_id" does not exist` on `booking_tokens_insert` policy. Remote `booking_tokens` table (from migration 0006) has no `user_id` column — only `id, token, resume_id, job_id, expires_at, used_at, created_at`. Also discovered `interviews`, `hire_outcomes`, `scorecard_responses`, `guest_links` have `account_id` on remote (not in 0013). Fixed by querying actual remote schema and updating policies to match.
   - **app_id INSERT failure (critical):** After migration 0017, `app_id` was `NOT NULL` with no DEFAULT and no trigger. Frontend never passes `app_id`. All INSERTs to 34 legacy tables would fail. Fixed by migration 0018 adding `DEFAULT get_app_id('rankora')` + `set_rankora_app_id()` BEFORE INSERT trigger to all affected tables.

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Root cause of "database not connected":** Legacy tables lacked `app_id` FK, preventing app-level RLS isolation — solved by migrations 0017 + 0018
   - **Two-layer fix needed:** Both the schema (app_id column + RLS) AND the default/trigger mechanism were required — migration 0017 fixed schema, migration 0018 fixed the auto-population
   - **Remote vs local schema drift:** The actual remote DB had tables created by migration 0006 (not 0013) for some tables — policies had to match actual remote schema, not local migration-defined schema
   - **13 views with no write support (PENDING):** Most compat views grant INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE but have zero INSTEAD OF triggers — every write through these views silently fails or returns PostgreSQL error. This is the main cause of "save failed" throughout the app.
   - **Frontend column mismatches (PENDING):** `useCandidateNotes` uses `job_id`/`author_id`/`note_type`/`mentions` — none exist in the underlying table. `useCandidateTags` uses `job_id` — doesn't exist. `usePipelineStages` uses `sort_order` but table has `position`.

   - **Fix `platform_config` view:** Restore `WHERE rpc.account_id = get_primary_account(auth.uid())` filter that was lost in migrations 0011/0014

# Plan: Add `app_id` to All Legacy Tables + Fix RLS Policies

## Context

Rankora's database has two generations of tables:
- **BUBS-era (`rankora_*`)**: 20 tables with `app_id` FK + RLS enforcing `has_app_access(account_id, app_id)`
- **Legacy (non-prefixed)**: 34 tables missing `app_id` — no app-level isolation, many have wide-open `true` RLS policies

This migration adds `app_id` to all 34 legacy tables, backfills existing rows, and replaces the weak RLS policies with proper `is_account_member() AND has_app_access()` checks matching the `rankora_*` pattern.

## Single Migration File

**File:** `supabase/migrations/2026XXXXXXXXXX_add_app_id_to_legacy_tables.sql`

### Part 1: Add `app_id` column to all 34 tables

For each table, the pattern is:
```sql
ALTER TABLE <table> ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS app_id uuid REFERENCES apps(id);
UPDATE <table> SET app_id = get_app_id('rankora') WHERE app_id IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE <table> ALTER COLUMN app_id SET NOT NULL;
```

**Category 1 — 23 tables with `account_id` (need `app_id` + composite index):**
1. `activity_log`
2. `agency_clients`
3. `agency_commissions`
4. `agency_communications`
5. `agency_contacts`
6. `agency_invoices`
7. `agency_mandates`
8. `agency_placements`
9. `availability_slots`
10. `guest_links`
11. `hire_outcomes`
12. `interviews`
13. `notifications`
14. `outreach_history`
15. `payments`
16. `scorecard_responses`
17. `scorecard_templates`
18. `sequences`
19. `stage_tracker`
20. `talent_pool`
21. `talent_pool_members`
22. `team_invitations`
23. `webhook_configs`

Each gets: `CREATE INDEX idx_<table>_account_app ON <table>(account_id, app_id);`

**Category 2 — 11 tables connected via FK chain (need `app_id` + single index):**
1. `booking_tokens`
2. `candidate_stages`
3. `career_subscribers`
4. `job_form_fields`
5. `job_views`
6. `outreach_log`
7. `sequence_enrollments`
8. `sequence_steps`
9. `stage_automations`
10. `stage_history`
11. `sms_logs`

Each gets: `CREATE INDEX idx_<table>_app ON <table>(app_id);`

### Part 2: Drop all existing RLS policies on these tables, then create proper ones

**Current state of RLS (problematic):**
- Many tables have 2-3 overlapping policies from migrations 0006, 0013, 0015
- 14+ tables have `USING (true)` SELECT — any authenticated user can read all rows
- Write policies only check `auth.uid() IS NOT NULL` — any user can write to any row

**New RLS pattern per table (matching `rankora_*` convention):**

For tables with `account_id`:
```sql
-- SELECT: must be account member with app access
CREATE POLICY <table>_select ON <table> FOR SELECT
  USING (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id));

-- INSERT: must be account member with app access, app must be rankora
CREATE POLICY <table>_insert ON <table> FOR INSERT
  WITH CHECK (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id)
              AND app_id = get_app_id('rankora'));

-- UPDATE: same as select
CREATE POLICY <table>_update ON <table> FOR UPDATE
  USING (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id));

-- DELETE: same as select
CREATE POLICY <table>_delete ON <table> FOR DELETE
  USING (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id));
```

**Special cases:**
- `notifications` — keep `user_id = auth.uid()` as primary check (user-scoped), add `app_id` check
- `sms_logs` — keep `user_id = auth.uid()` as primary check, add `app_id` check
- `payments` — keep `user_id = auth.uid() OR is_account_member(account_id)`, add `app_id` check
- `booking_tokens`, `job_views`, `career_subscribers` — SELECT stays public (no auth required for public-facing pages), but INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE require account membership + app access
- `job_form_fields`, `stage_automations` — SELECT public for application forms, writes require membership
- `talent_pool_members` — needs JOIN-based check through `talent_pool.account_id`

### Part 3: Composite indexes

Add `(account_id, app_id)` composite indexes to all Category 1 tables and `(app_id)` indexes to Category 2 tables for RLS performance.

## Files to Modify

1. **New file:** `supabase/migrations/20260413000001_add_app_id_to_legacy_tables.sql` — the full migration
2. **No frontend changes needed** — RLS enforces app_id server-side; client queries already filter by account_id and RLS adds the app_id check transparently

## Verification

1. Apply migration: `supabase db push` (or `supabase db reset` on develop)
2. Verify all 34 tables have `app_id` column: `SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE column_name = 'app_id'`
3. Verify no table has `USING (true)` policies left: check `pg_policies` view
4. Test existing features in dev:
   - Dashboard loads (activity_log, notifications)
   - Tasks page works (rankora_tasks already had app_id)
   - Team/invitations work (team_invitations)
   - Talent pool page works
   - Sequences page works
   - Payments/billing display correctly
5. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` — should pass (no frontend type changes)
6. Run `npx vitest run` — should pass
