-- ============================================================================
-- 20260420000005_bubs_compat_views.sql
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Compatibility views that expose the new BUBS rankora_* tables under
-- the OLD table names the frontend is still using.
--
-- This is a PRAGMATIC bridge so the existing ~30 frontend hooks and
-- ~45 edge functions continue to function while the codebase is
-- gradually migrated to query rankora_* / accounts / account_users
-- directly. Each view forwards to the new table.
--
-- These views are security_invoker = true so RLS on the underlying
-- rankora_* tables is enforced based on the CALLING user, not the
-- view owner. This is CRITICAL — without security_invoker, any
-- authenticated user could read any account's data through the view.
--
-- RULES for consumers of these views:
--  - Read paths work automatically (SELECT flows through RLS)
--  - Write paths (INSERT/UPDATE) are proxied via INSTEAD OF triggers
--    that inject app_id + account_id from the current auth context
--  - The views are marked @deprecated. New code should write directly
--    against the rankora_* tables with explicit account_id.
-- ============================================================================


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 1. `profiles` view — synthesized from users + accounts + plans
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The old profiles table held per-user billing state: credits, plan,
-- subscription_ends_at, inbox_email, email_enabled, auto_rank_enabled.
--
-- In BUBS, billing lives on the account, not the user. A user with
-- multiple accounts has different credit balances per account. We
-- expose the PRIMARY account's state here so useAuthNext continues
-- working with a single profile object.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW profiles
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  u.id                                              AS user_id,
  u.id                                              AS id,
  u.email,
  u.full_name,
  u.avatar_url,
  -- Primary account's id (used as the workspace identifier)
  pa.id                                             AS account_id,
  pa.id                                             AS team_id,  -- legacy alias
  pa.name                                           AS team_name,
  -- Inbox email for the rankora platform config
  NULL::text                                        AS inbox_email,
  -- Current plan slug (from account_app_access → plans)
  COALESCE(pl.slug, 'free')                         AS plan,
  -- Credits synthesized from limits_json (ai_credits_per_month)
  COALESCE((pl.limits_json->>'ai_credits_per_month')::int, 30) AS credits,
  COALESCE((pl.limits_json->>'ai_credits_per_month')::int, 30) AS subscription_credits,
  0                                                 AS topup_credits,
  0                                                 AS bonus_credits,
  -- Per-account rankora settings
  COALESCE(rpc.email_ingestion_enabled, false)      AS email_enabled,
  COALESCE(rpc.auto_rank_enabled, true)             AS auto_rank_enabled,
  aaa.expires_at                                    AS subscription_ends_at,
  NULL::text                                        AS dodo_subscription_id,
  u.created_at,
  u.updated_at
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT a.*
  FROM account_users au
  JOIN accounts a ON a.id = au.account_id
  WHERE au.user_id = u.id
  ORDER BY
    CASE au.role WHEN 'owner' THEN 1 WHEN 'admin' THEN 2 WHEN 'member' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END,
    au.created_at ASC
  LIMIT 1
) pa ON true
LEFT JOIN account_app_access aaa
  ON aaa.account_id = pa.id AND aaa.app_id = get_app_id('rankora')
LEFT JOIN plans pl ON pl.id = aaa.plan_id
LEFT JOIN rankora_platform_config rpc ON rpc.account_id = pa.id;

GRANT SELECT ON profiles TO authenticated, anon;

COMMENT ON VIEW profiles IS
  '@deprecated Compat view bridging old profiles table to new BUBS schema. Migrate consumers to query users + account_app_access + plans directly.';


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 2. `user_roles` view — admin is determined by account_users.role
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Old user_roles was a global app_role enum table with admin/user.
-- In BUBS, "admin" means account owner/admin, but the global admin
-- (for the /admin Rankora panel) is a separate concept. We expose
-- anyone who owns the account with email matching a boldteq.com
-- or rankora.co domain as a global admin for legacy compat.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW user_roles
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  u.id AS user_id,
  CASE
    -- Until real admin roles are added, treat owners of the first
    -- account with boldteq/rankora email as the global admin
    WHEN u.email LIKE '%@boldteq.com' OR u.email LIKE '%@rankora.co' THEN 'admin'
    ELSE 'user'
  END AS role
FROM users u;

GRANT SELECT ON user_roles TO authenticated;

COMMENT ON VIEW user_roles IS
  '@deprecated Compat view. Global admin is now derived from email domain. Real RBAC lives in account_users.role for per-account permissions.';


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 3. `jobs` view → rankora_jobs
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW jobs
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id                        AS user_id,  -- legacy field name; actually account
  account_id                        AS team_id,
  account_id,
  app_id,
  created_by,
  title,
  job_description,
  jd_analysis_json,
  dynamic_weights_json,
  scoring_weights,
  status,
  inbox_email,
  jd_embedding,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_jobs;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON jobs TO authenticated;

-- INSTEAD OF INSERT trigger: writes to rankora_jobs with auto-filled app_id
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION jobs_insert_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
DECLARE
  v_account_id uuid;
BEGIN
  -- Resolve the caller's primary account if not provided
  v_account_id := COALESCE(NEW.account_id, NEW.team_id, get_primary_account(auth.uid()));

  INSERT INTO rankora_jobs (
    id, app_id, account_id, created_by,
    title, job_description, jd_analysis_json, dynamic_weights_json,
    scoring_weights, status, inbox_email, jd_embedding
  ) VALUES (
    COALESCE(NEW.id, gen_random_uuid()),
    get_app_id('rankora'),
    v_account_id,
    COALESCE(NEW.created_by, auth.uid()),
    NEW.title,
    NEW.job_description,
    NEW.jd_analysis_json,
    NEW.dynamic_weights_json,
    COALESCE(NEW.scoring_weights, '{"must": 0.6, "nice": 0.3, "optional": 0.1}'::jsonb),
    COALESCE(NEW.status, 'pending'),
    NEW.inbox_email,
    NEW.jd_embedding
  );
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER jobs_insert_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF INSERT ON jobs
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION jobs_insert_trigger();


-- INSTEAD OF UPDATE trigger
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION jobs_update_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  UPDATE rankora_jobs SET
    title                = NEW.title,
    job_description      = NEW.job_description,
    jd_analysis_json     = NEW.jd_analysis_json,
    dynamic_weights_json = NEW.dynamic_weights_json,
    scoring_weights      = NEW.scoring_weights,
    status               = NEW.status,
    inbox_email          = NEW.inbox_email,
    jd_embedding         = NEW.jd_embedding
  WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER jobs_update_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF UPDATE ON jobs
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION jobs_update_trigger();


-- INSTEAD OF DELETE trigger
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION jobs_delete_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM rankora_jobs WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN OLD;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER jobs_delete_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF DELETE ON jobs
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION jobs_delete_trigger();


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 4. `resumes` view → rankora_resumes
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW resumes
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  job_id,
  account_id        AS user_id,  -- legacy field alias
  account_id,
  app_id,
  created_by,
  filename,
  file_path,
  file_size_bytes,
  candidate_name,
  candidate_email,
  candidate_phone,
  candidate_location,
  parsed_json,
  parsed_text,
  embedding,
  status,
  source,
  created_at
FROM rankora_resumes;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON resumes TO authenticated;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION resumes_insert_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
DECLARE
  v_account_id uuid;
BEGIN
  -- Resolve account from the job if not provided
  v_account_id := COALESCE(
    NEW.account_id,
    (SELECT account_id FROM rankora_jobs WHERE id = NEW.job_id),
    get_primary_account(auth.uid())
  );

  INSERT INTO rankora_resumes (
    id, app_id, account_id, job_id, created_by,
    filename, file_path, file_size_bytes,
    candidate_name, candidate_email, candidate_phone, candidate_location,
    parsed_json, parsed_text, embedding, status, source
  ) VALUES (
    COALESCE(NEW.id, gen_random_uuid()),
    get_app_id('rankora'),
    v_account_id,
    NEW.job_id,
    COALESCE(NEW.created_by, auth.uid()),
    NEW.filename,
    NEW.file_path,
    NEW.file_size_bytes,
    NEW.candidate_name,
    NEW.candidate_email,
    NEW.candidate_phone,
    NEW.candidate_location,
    NEW.parsed_json,
    NEW.parsed_text,
    NEW.embedding,
    COALESCE(NEW.status, 'pending'),
    NEW.source
  );
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER resumes_insert_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF INSERT ON resumes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION resumes_insert_trigger();


CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION resumes_update_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  UPDATE rankora_resumes SET
    filename            = NEW.filename,
    file_path           = NEW.file_path,
    file_size_bytes     = NEW.file_size_bytes,
    candidate_name      = NEW.candidate_name,
    candidate_email     = NEW.candidate_email,
    candidate_phone     = NEW.candidate_phone,
    candidate_location  = NEW.candidate_location,
    parsed_json         = NEW.parsed_json,
    parsed_text         = NEW.parsed_text,
    embedding           = NEW.embedding,
    status              = NEW.status,
    source              = NEW.source
  WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER resumes_update_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF UPDATE ON resumes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION resumes_update_trigger();


CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION resumes_delete_trigger()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM rankora_resumes WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN OLD;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER resumes_delete_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF DELETE ON resumes
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION resumes_delete_trigger();


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 5. `results` view → rankora_results
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW results
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  job_id,
  resume_id,
  account_id,
  app_id,
  overall_score,
  skill_score,
  experience_score,
  education_score,
  category_scores_json,
  confidence,
  hard_fit,
  missing_skills,
  matched_must_haves,
  missing_must_haves,
  strengths_json,
  gaps_json,
  explanation_json,
  interview_questions,
  scoring_version,
  model_name,
  assigned_to,
  pipeline_stage,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_results;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON results TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 6. `teams` view → accounts (legacy alias for agency/team hub code)
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW teams
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  slug,
  owner_user_id,
  owner_user_id AS created_by,
  billing_email,
  status,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM accounts;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON teams TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 7. `team_members` view → account_users
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW team_members
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  user_id,
  role::text,
  created_at
FROM account_users;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON team_members TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 8. `platform_config` view → rankora_platform_config (global singleton)
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The old platform_config was a single-row global table. In BUBS
-- it's per-account. This view picks the caller's primary account's
-- config so single-row SELECTs still work.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW platform_config
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  rpc.*,
  'rankora.co' AS inbound_email_domain,  -- hardcoded legacy field
  get_app_id('rankora') AS app_id
FROM rankora_platform_config rpc
WHERE rpc.account_id = get_primary_account(auth.uid());

GRANT SELECT, UPDATE ON platform_config TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- 9. `plans` is already a real table — expose backward-compatible shape
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- The old code expects plans to have: id, name, price, credits,
-- billing_type, active, dodo_product_id, is_trial, features.
-- The new plans table has: price_cents, limits_json (no dodo ids yet).
-- We add computed columns via a view.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_legacy_plans
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  p.id,

4	-- Additional compat layer for the admin panel. The frontend admin tabs
5	-- query a dozen tables that don't exist in BUBS yet (payments,
6	-- ranking_config, seo_settings, prompt_versions, etc.). Rather than
7	-- rewriting all those admin tabs right now, we create:
8	--

11	-- 2. Stub tables for features that aren't re-implemented yet
12	--    (payments, ranking_config, seo_settings, prompt_versions,

-- ============================================================================
-- 20260420000006_bubs_admin_compat.sql
-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Additional compat layer for the admin panel. The frontend admin tabs
-- query a dozen tables that don't exist in BUBS yet (payments,
-- ranking_config, seo_settings, prompt_versions, etc.). Rather than
-- rewriting all those admin tabs right now, we create:
--
-- 1. Views that forward existing BUBS tables under legacy names
--    (e.g. changelog → rankora_changelog)
-- 2. Stub tables for features that aren't re-implemented yet
--    (payments, ranking_config, seo_settings, prompt_versions,
--    integrations, email_templates, email_ingest_logs)
--
-- All stub tables start empty. Admin tabs will render "No data" which
-- is honest — these features need proper BUBS rewrites.
-- ============================================================================


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- changelog view → rankora_changelog
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW changelog
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  version,
  title,
  description,
  category,
  status,
  published_at,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_changelog;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON changelog TO authenticated, anon;

-- INSTEAD OF triggers so admin panel can still write to changelog
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION changelog_insert_trigger()
RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO rankora_changelog (
    id, app_id, version, title, description, category, status, published_at
  ) VALUES (
    COALESCE(NEW.id, gen_random_uuid()),
    get_app_id('rankora'),
    NEW.version,
    NEW.title,
    NEW.description,
    NEW.category,
    COALESCE(NEW.status, 'draft'),
    NEW.published_at
  );
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER changelog_insert_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF INSERT ON changelog
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION changelog_insert_trigger();

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION changelog_update_trigger()
RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  UPDATE rankora_changelog SET
    version      = NEW.version,
    title        = NEW.title,
    description  = NEW.description,
    category     = NEW.category,
    status       = NEW.status,
    published_at = NEW.published_at
  WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER changelog_update_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF UPDATE ON changelog
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION changelog_update_trigger();

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION changelog_delete_trigger()
RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM rankora_changelog WHERE id = OLD.id;
  RETURN OLD;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER changelog_delete_instead_of
  INSTEAD OF DELETE ON changelog
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION changelog_delete_trigger();

account_id AS user_id,

  body AS content,
  body,

  updated_at

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON candidate_notes TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- candidate_tags view → rankora_candidate_tags
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW candidate_tags
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS user_id,
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  resume_id,
  created_by,
  tag,
  color,
  created_at
FROM rankora_candidate_tags;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON candidate_tags TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- job_pipeline_stages view → rankora_pipeline_stages
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW job_pipeline_stages
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  name,
  slug,
  color,
  position,
  is_default,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_pipeline_stages;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON job_pipeline_stages TO authenticated;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- applications view → rankora_applications
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW applications
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS user_id,
  account_id AS team_id,
  account_id,
  job_id,
  candidate_name,
  candidate_email,
  candidate_phone,
  resume_path,
  custom_fields_json,
  source,
  status,
  created_at,
  updated_at
FROM rankora_applications;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON applications TO authenticated, anon;


-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- api_keys view → rankora_api_keys
-- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW api_keys
WITH (security_invoker = true) AS
SELECT
  id,
  account_id AS user_id,
  account_id,
  created_by,
  name,
  key_prefix,
  key_hash,
  last_used_at,
  expires_at,
  revoked_at,
  created_at
FROM rankora_api_keys;

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON api_keys TO authenticated;

  dodo_checkout_session_id text,

content.text:
The `useState` lazy initializer was calling `localStorage.getItem()` synchronously — which works on the client but throws/returns nothing on the server. So SSR rendered `data-state="expanded"` (defaultOpen=true) while the client immediately hydrated with `data-state="collapsed"` (from localStorage), causing React to log the mismatch.

Fix: initialize state with `defaultOpen` on both sides so SSR and initial client paint match, then apply the persisted localStorage value in `useEffect` after mount. The sidebar will briefly flash to the correct collapsed state on load, but that's a one-frame transition with no visual artifact since it happens before the user sees anything meaningful.

For each table, the pattern is:
```sql
ALTER TABLE <table> ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS app_id uuid REFERENCES apps(id);
UPDATE <table> SET app_id = get_app_id('rankora') WHERE app_id IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE <table> ALTER COLUMN app_id SET NOT NULL;
```

**Category 1 — 23 tables with `account_id` (need `app_id` + composite index):**
1. `activity_log`
2. `agency_clients`
3. `agency_commissions`
4. `agency_communications`
5. `agency_contacts`
6. `agency_invoices`
7. `agency_mandates`
8. `agency_placements`
9. `availability_slots`
10. `guest_links`
11. `hire_outcomes`
12. `interviews`
13. `notifications`
14. `outreach_history`
15. `payments`
16. `scorecard_responses`
17. `scorecard_templates`
18. `sequences`
19. `stage_tracker`
20. `talent_pool`
21. `talent_pool_members`
22. `team_invitations`
23. `webhook_configs`

Each gets: `CREATE INDEX idx_<table>_account_app ON <table>(account_id, app_id);`

**Category 2 — 11 tables connected via FK chain (need `app_id` + single index):**
1. `booking_tokens`
2. `candidate_stages`
3. `career_subscribers`
4. `job_form_fields`
5. `job_views`
6. `outreach_log`
7. `sequence_enrollments`
8. `sequence_steps`
9. `stage_automations`
10. `stage_history`
11. `sms_logs`

Each gets: `CREATE INDEX idx_<table>_app ON <table>(app_id);`

### Part 2: Drop all existing RLS policies on these tables, then create proper ones

**Current state of RLS (problematic):**
- Many tables have 2-3 overlapping policies from migrations 0006, 0013, 0015
- 14+ tables have `USING (true)` SELECT — any authenticated user can read all rows
- Write policies only check `auth.uid() IS NOT NULL` — any user can write to any row

**New RLS pattern per table (matching `rankora_*` convention):**

For tables with `account_id`:
```sql
-- SELECT: must be account member with app access
CREATE POLICY <table>_select ON <table> FOR SELECT
  USING (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id));

-- INSERT: must be account member with app access, app must be rankora
CREATE POLICY <table>_insert ON <table> FOR INSERT
  WITH CHECK (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id)
              AND app_id = get_app_id('rankora'));

-- UPDATE: same as select
CREATE POLICY <table>_update ON <table> FOR UPDATE
  USING (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id));

-- DELETE: same as select
CREATE POLICY <table>_delete ON <table> FOR DELETE
  USING (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id));
```

**Special cases:**
- `notifications` — keep `user_id = auth.uid()` as primary check (user-scoped), add `app_id` check
- `sms_logs` — keep `user_id = auth.uid()` as primary check, add `app_id` check
- `payments` — keep `user_id = auth.uid() OR is_account_member(account_id)`, add `app_id` check

- `job_form_fields`, `stage_automations` — SELECT public for application forms, writes require membership
- `talent_pool_members` — needs JOIN-based check through `talent_pool.account_id`

### Part 3: Composite indexes

Add `(account_id, app_id)` composite indexes to all Category 1 tables and `(app_id)` indexes to Category 2 tables for RLS performance.

## RLS Policy Audit Summary: Write-Path Blockers in Rankora

Based on migrations 0017, 0018, and 0019, here are the RLS policies that could plausibly block writes:

---

### CRITICAL: Missing account_id Defaults (Category 1 Tables)

**Tables with INSERT policies requiring `is_account_member(account_id)` but NO DEFAULT on account_id:**

| Table | INSERT Policy | Risk |
|-------|---------------|------|
| agency_clients | `is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id) AND app_id = get_app_id('rankora')` | BLOCKER: If frontend doesn't pass account_id, WITH CHECK fails |
| agency_commissions | Same | BLOCKER |
| agency_communications | Same | BLOCKER |
| agency_contacts | Same | BLOCKER |
| agency_invoices | Same | BLOCKER |
| agency_mandates | Same | BLOCKER |
| agency_placements | Same | BLOCKER |
| guest_links | Same | BLOCKER |
| hire_outcomes | Same | BLOCKER |
| interviews | Same | BLOCKER |
| outreach_history | Same | BLOCKER |
| scorecard_responses | Same | BLOCKER |
| scorecard_templates | Same | BLOCKER |
| sequences | Same | BLOCKER |
| stage_tracker | Same | BLOCKER |
| talent_pool | Same | BLOCKER |
| team_invitations | Same (with `is_account_admin`) | BLOCKER |
| webhook_configs | Same | BLOCKER |

**Status:** These are SAFE because migration 0018 adds `DEFAULT get_app_id('rankora')` + BEFORE INSERT trigger `set_rankora_app_id()`. However, `account_id` has NO DEFAULT. If frontend doesn't pass `account_id`, RLS will fail at WITH CHECK evaluation.

---

### SAFE (Documented Edge Cases)

**1. activity_log, notifications, payments, availability_slots**
- Have DUAL auth paths: `user_id = auth.uid() OR account_id + access checks`
- Frontend can pass `user_id` or `account_id`; INSERT succeeds either way

**2. talent_pool_members**
- No account_id column; relies on FK subquery:
  ```sql
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM talent_pool tp WHERE tp.id = pool_id AND is_account_member(tp.account_id))
  ```
- Safe: subquery checks the parent record's account_id

**3. team_invitations**
- INSERT requires `is_account_admin(account_id)` (stricter than member check)
- Same account_id issue as Category 1, but admin role makes blocker acceptable (intentional gate)

---

### View-with-INSTEAD OF Triggers (0019)

**Migration 0019 adds INSERT triggers that resolve account_id:**

| View | Trigger Resolves | Underlying Policy |
|------|------------------|-------------------|
| tasks | `v_account_id := COALESCE(NEW.account_id, NEW.team_id, NEW.user_id, get_primary_account(auth.uid()))` | rankora_tasks: `is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id) AND app_id = get_app_id('rankora') AND created_by = auth.uid()` |
| candidate_notes | Same pattern | rankora_candidate_notes: Same, + `created_by = auth.uid()` |
| candidate_tags | Same pattern | rankora_candidate_tags: Same pattern |
| career_page_config | Same pattern | rankora_career_pages: `is_account_admin(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id) AND app_id = get_app_id('rankora')` |
| feature_requests | `COALESCE(NEW.user_id, auth.uid())` (no account_id needed) | rankora_feature_requests: `created_by = auth.uid() AND app_id = get_app_id('rankora')` |
| applications | Resolves `v_account_id` via FK: `(SELECT account_id FROM rankora_jobs WHERE id = NEW.job_id)` | rankora_applications: SELECT only; INSERT via service role |
| api_keys | `v_account_id := COALESCE(NEW.account_id, NEW.user_id, get_primary_account(auth.uid()))` | rankora_api_keys: `is_account_admin(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id) AND app_id = get_app_id('rankora')` |
| team_members | `v_account_id := COALESCE(NEW.account_id, NEW.team_id, get_primary_account(auth.uid()))` | account_users (not shown): Upsert by PK (account_id, user_id) |
| teams | UPDATE/DELETE only; no INSERT trigger | accounts: admin-only |
| pipeline_stages | `v_account_id := COALESCE(NEW.account_id, NEW.team_id, get_primary_account(auth.uid()))` | rankora_pipeline_stages: `is_account_admin(account_id) AND app_id = get_app_id('rankora')` |

**Status:** SAFE — triggers fire BEFORE RLS check, resolving missing columns. `get_primary_account(auth.uid())` is the fallback.

---

### Real Tables Direct Writes (Not Protected by Views)

**Tables with INSERT to authenticated, no view abstraction:**

1. **booking_tokens** — INSERT: `app_id = get_app_id('rankora') AND auth.uid() IS NOT NULL`
   - No account_id column; gate is `auth.uid()` only. Safe.

2. **candidate_stages** — INSERT: `app_id = get_app_id('rankora')`
   - No auth.uid() gate; anon can write. Acceptable (lightweight staging table).

3. **career_subscribers** — INSERT: `app_id = get_app_id('rankora')`
   - Anon can subscribe. Acceptable (public signup).

4. **job_form_fields** — INSERT: `app_id = get_app_id('rankora')`
   - Anon can create. Acceptable (public form collection).

5. **job_views** — INSERT: `app_id = get_app_id('rankora')`
   - Anon tracking. Acceptable.

6. **outreach_log, sequence_enrollments, sequence_steps, stage_automations, stage_history** — INSERT: `app_id = get_app_id('rankora')`
   - No account context. Safe (internal log-only tables; no account_id column).

7. **sms_logs** — INSERT: `app_id = get_app_id('rankora')`
   - Safe.

---

### App ID Trigger Verification

**Migration 0018 sets up:**
```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION set_rankora_app_id()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.app_id IS NULL THEN
    NEW.app_id := get_app_id('rankora');
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;
```

**Postgres RLS execution order:** DEFAULT → BEFORE INSERT trigger → RLS WITH CHECK.
- app_id will be populated by trigger before RLS evaluates `app_id = get_app_id('rankora')`. ✓ Safe.

---

### Summary: Write Blockers

**GENUINE BLOCKERS (frontend must pass account_id):**
- 17 legacy tables (agency_*, guest_links, hire_outcomes, interviews, outreach_history, scorecard_*, sequences, stage_tracker, talent_pool, team_invitations, webhook_configs)
- RLS requires `is_account_member(account_id)` but column has no DEFAULT
- **Mitigation:** Frontend should always pass account_id, OR add DEFAULT + trigger to legacy tables (0018 only covers 34 specific tables, check if all 17 are in the list — they are)

**SAFE (via triggers):**
- All view-backed writes (tasks, candidate_notes, candidate_tags, applications, etc.)

**SAFE (auth gate only):**
- Booking tokens, candidate_stages, career_subscribers, job_form_fields, job_views, outreach_log, sms_logs, etc.

## Context

But the 3-way audit just completed surfaced a long tail of residual save failures across the app — column mismatches, missing views, views without triggers, upsert conflicts with no unique constraint, NOT NULL `account_id` with no frontend-passed value, and dead admin tables.

This plan hands Dato (Database Architect) a single consolidated fix pass across migration + hook layers, then uses Playwright to verify flows end-to-end on `localhost:8080`.

**Scope: every write path in the app must round-trip successfully.**

---

## Phase 1: Migration 0020 — Residual DB Fixes

**File:** `supabase/migrations/20260420000020_comprehensive_save_path_fixes.sql`

### Part 1.1 — Add INSTEAD OF triggers for remaining views without them

Views currently granted INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE but still missing triggers post-0019:

- **`profiles`** — INSTEAD OF UPDATE trigger:
  - `avatar_url` → `UPDATE users SET avatar_url = NEW.avatar_url WHERE id = OLD.user_id`
  - `email_enabled` → `UPDATE rankora_platform_config SET email_ingestion_enabled = NEW.email_enabled WHERE account_id = get_primary_account(auth.uid())`
  - `full_name` → `UPDATE users SET full_name = NEW.full_name WHERE id = OLD.user_id`
  - Used by: [Profile.tsx:186](src/legacy-pages/Profile.tsx#L186), [Profile.tsx:209](src/legacy-pages/Profile.tsx#L209), [EmailInboxCard.tsx:50](src/components/settings/EmailInboxCard.tsx#L50)

- **`admin_audit_logs`** — INSTEAD OF INSERT trigger:
  - Map `admin_user_id → user_id`, `details → changes_json`
  - INSERT into `audit_logs` with `action LIKE 'admin.%'` preserved
  - Used by: [auditLog.ts:23](src/lib/auditLog.ts#L23)

- **`feature_request_votes`** — no frontend direct writes (uses RPC). **Skip**.

### Part 1.2 — Fix `candidate_stages` schema mismatch

[useStageTracker.ts:68](src/hooks/useStageTracker.ts#L68) upserts with columns `updated_at`, `updated_by`, `resume_id`, `job_id`, `stage` — but table has `moved_at`, `moved_by`. Upsert uses `onConflict: "resume_id,job_id"` with no unique constraint.

- Add columns: `updated_at timestamptz DEFAULT now()`, `updated_by uuid REFERENCES users(id)`
- Keep legacy `moved_at`/`moved_by` for backward compat (backfill one from the other via trigger)
- Add `UNIQUE (resume_id, job_id)` constraint to support the upsert

### Part 1.3 — Fix `hire_outcomes` schema mismatch

[useHireOutcomes.ts:99](src/hooks/useHireOutcomes.ts#L99) upserts with `recommendation`, `updated_at`, `onConflict: "resume_id,job_id"` — table is missing all three.

- Add columns: `recommendation text`, `updated_at timestamptz DEFAULT now()`
- Add `UNIQUE (resume_id, job_id)` constraint

### Part 1.4 — Fix `sequences` / sequence_steps missing account_id default

[useSequences.ts:213](src/hooks/useSequences.ts#L213) inserts with `user_id` but table has `created_by`, and `account_id` is NOT NULL with no default.

Tables: `agency_clients`, `agency_commissions`, `agency_communications`, `agency_contacts`, `agency_invoices`, `agency_mandates`, `agency_placements`, `guest_links`, `hire_outcomes`, `interviews`, `outreach_history`, `scorecard_responses`, `scorecard_templates`, `sequences`, `stage_tracker`, `talent_pool`, `webhook_configs`.

Strategy: shared BEFORE INSERT trigger function `set_rankora_account_id()`:
```sql
IF NEW.account_id IS NULL THEN
  NEW.account_id := COALESCE(NEW.team_id, get_primary_account(auth.uid()));
END IF;
```
Applied alongside the existing `set_rankora_app_id()` trigger on each table.

### Part 1.6 — Fix `outreach_log` missing job_id column

[ContactStrip.tsx:28](src/components/candidate/ContactStrip.tsx#L28) inserts `job_id` into `outreach_log`. Table has no `job_id`.

- Add `job_id uuid REFERENCES rankora_jobs(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`

### Part 1.7 — Fix `guest_links` NOT NULL token

Hook [GuestLinkDialog.tsx:89](src/components/GuestLinkDialog.tsx#L89) inserts `job_id, team_id, created_by, label` — doesn't pass `token` which is NOT NULL. Table has `token text UNIQUE NOT NULL DEFAULT encode(gen_random_bytes(32), 'hex')` — so default fires. But `label` isn't a column.

- Add `label text` column
- Ensure `used_at` column exists (0006 has it)

### Part 1.8 — Create admin `plans` compat layer

[PlansTab.tsx](src/components/admin/PlansTab.tsx) writes 13× to `plans` with columns `dodo_product_id`, `dodo_credit_entitlement_id`, `price`, `credits`, `active`, `is_trial`, `features`. BUBS `plans` table has different schema.

Two options — choose one:
- **A.** Add the missing columns to the real `plans` table: `dodo_product_id text`, `dodo_credit_entitlement_id text`, `is_trial boolean DEFAULT false`. Compute `price/credits/active/features` via trigger → `price_cents/limits_json/status`.
- **B.** Replace `plans` name with view `plans` that maps to `v_legacy_plans` (already exists from 0005) + INSTEAD OF INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers that write to underlying `plans` base table.

**Decision:** Option A. Simpler. One ALTER TABLE + one BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger that keeps `price_cents` in sync with `price*100`, `status` in sync with `active`, and `limits_json->>'ai_credits_per_month'` in sync with `credits`.

### Part 1.9 — Fix `applications` column exposure

Audit found `ApplicationsTab.tsx:105` selects `name, email, phone, linkedin_url, resume_filename, auto_disqualified, disqualify_reason, custom_fields`. Migration 0019 added these to the `applications` view and `rankora_applications` table — verify they made it through (migration was applied, but double-check via `SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = 'rankora_applications'`).

No migration change needed if already applied.

- Line 190 (interviews insert): missing `account_id`. The Phase 1.5 shared trigger will auto-resolve from `get_primary_account(auth.uid())`. No frontend change needed.

- Audit that every `.on("postgres_changes", { filter: "col=eq.val" })` references a column that actually exists in the table the subscription targets. Key suspects:
  - [useTasks.tsx](src/hooks/useTasks.tsx) — realtime on `rankora_tasks` or `tasks`?
  - [useHireOutcomes.ts](src/hooks/useHireOutcomes.ts) — realtime on `hire_outcomes` with which filter?
  - Various page-level realtime channels

Dato must search `.on("postgres_changes"` in `src/**` and verify each filter column exists on the target table. **Fix any mismatches.**

Writes to `email_ingest_logs`. Migration 0018 added `app_id` + trigger. Verify.

- Possibly: realtime filter fixes in any hook found with broken subscription (Phase 2.8)

4. Fix hooks per Phase 2 (only useSequences.ts definitely, others only if migration doesn't fully cover)

# Plan: Add `app_id` to All Legacy Tables + Fix RLS Policies

## Context

Rankora's database has two generations of tables:
- **BUBS-era (`rankora_*`)**: 20 tables with `app_id` FK + RLS enforcing `has_app_access(account_id, app_id)`
- **Legacy (non-prefixed)**: 34 tables missing `app_id` — no app-level isolation, many have wide-open `true` RLS policies

This migration adds `app_id` to all 34 legacy tables, backfills existing rows, and replaces the weak RLS policies with proper `is_account_member() AND has_app_access()` checks matching the `rankora_*` pattern.

## Single Migration File

**File:** `supabase/migrations/2026XXXXXXXXXX_add_app_id_to_legacy_tables.sql`

### Part 1: Add `app_id` column to all 34 tables

For each table, the pattern is:
```sql
ALTER TABLE <table> ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS app_id uuid REFERENCES apps(id);
UPDATE <table> SET app_id = get_app_id('rankora') WHERE app_id IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE <table> ALTER COLUMN app_id SET NOT NULL;
```

**Category 1 — 23 tables with `account_id` (need `app_id` + composite index):**
1. `activity_log`
2. `agency_clients`
3. `agency_commissions`
4. `agency_communications`
5. `agency_contacts`
6. `agency_invoices`
7. `agency_mandates`
8. `agency_placements`
9. `availability_slots`
10. `guest_links`
11. `hire_outcomes`
12. `interviews`
13. `notifications`
14. `outreach_history`
15. `payments`
16. `scorecard_responses`
17. `scorecard_templates`
18. `sequences`
19. `stage_tracker`
20. `talent_pool`
21. `talent_pool_members`
22. `team_invitations`
23. `webhook_configs`

Each gets: `CREATE INDEX idx_<table>_account_app ON <table>(account_id, app_id);`

**Category 2 — 11 tables connected via FK chain (need `app_id` + single index):**
1. `booking_tokens`
2. `candidate_stages`
3. `career_subscribers`
4. `job_form_fields`
5. `job_views`
6. `outreach_log`
7. `sequence_enrollments`
8. `sequence_steps`
9. `stage_automations`
10. `stage_history`
11. `sms_logs`

Each gets: `CREATE INDEX idx_<table>_app ON <table>(app_id);`

### Part 2: Drop all existing RLS policies on these tables, then create proper ones

**Current state of RLS (problematic):**
- Many tables have 2-3 overlapping policies from migrations 0006, 0013, 0015
- 14+ tables have `USING (true)` SELECT — any authenticated user can read all rows
- Write policies only check `auth.uid() IS NOT NULL` — any user can write to any row

**New RLS pattern per table (matching `rankora_*` convention):**

For tables with `account_id`:
```sql
-- SELECT: must be account member with app access
CREATE POLICY <table>_select ON <table> FOR SELECT
  USING (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id));

-- INSERT: must be account member with app access, app must be rankora
CREATE POLICY <table>_insert ON <table> FOR INSERT
  WITH CHECK (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id)
              AND app_id = get_app_id('rankora'));

-- UPDATE: same as select
CREATE POLICY <table>_update ON <table> FOR UPDATE
  USING (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id));

-- DELETE: same as select
CREATE POLICY <table>_delete ON <table> FOR DELETE
  USING (is_account_member(account_id) AND has_app_access(account_id, app_id));
```

**Special cases:**
- `notifications` — keep `user_id = auth.uid()` as primary check (user-scoped), add `app_id` check
- `sms_logs` — keep `user_id = auth.uid()` as primary check, add `app_id` check
- `payments` — keep `user_id = auth.uid() OR is_account_member(account_id)`, add `app_id` check
- `booking_tokens`, `job_views`, `career_subscribers` — SELECT stays public (no auth required for public-facing pages), but INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE require account membership + app access
- `job_form_fields`, `stage_automations` — SELECT public for application forms, writes require membership
- `talent_pool_members` — needs JOIN-based check through `talent_pool.account_id`

### Part 3: Composite indexes

Add `(account_id, app_id)` composite indexes to all Category 1 tables and `(app_id)` indexes to Category 2 tables for RLS performance.

## Files to Modify

1. **New file:** `supabase/migrations/20260413000001_add_app_id_to_legacy_tables.sql` — the full migration
2. **No frontend changes needed** — RLS enforces app_id server-side; client queries already filter by account_id and RLS adds the app_id check transparently

## Verification

1. Apply migration: `supabase db push` (or `supabase db reset` on develop)
2. Verify all 34 tables have `app_id` column: `SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE column_name = 'app_id'`
3. Verify no table has `USING (true)` policies left: check `pg_policies` view
4. Test existing features in dev:
   - Dashboard loads (activity_log, notifications)
   - Tasks page works (rankora_tasks already had app_id)
   - Team/invitations work (team_invitations)
   - Talent pool page works
   - Sequences page works
   - Payments/billing display correctly
5. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` — should pass (no frontend type changes)
6. Run `npx vitest run` — should pass

The empty-object error was Supabase swallowing a PostgREST error with three simultaneous problems:
1. `agency_placements` stub only had 7 columns — the hook selected 8 others (`client_id`, `candidate_name/email`, `salary`, `fee_amount`, `start_date`, `guarantee_days`, `guarantee_expires_at`) that didn't exist

3. No `client_id` FK existed for PostgREST to embed `agency_clients(name)`

Migration 0021 adds all missing columns + `client_id` FK + a `job_title` alias column with a bidirectional sync trigger so both names always match. The hook now uses explicit FK constraint names in the embed (so it works even if PostgREST's schema cache is stale) and unpacks error `message/details/hint/code` into the console log so future errors aren't just `{}`.

## **SNAPSHOT: Rankora Admin Panel Redesign**

### **1. Admin Panel Current Shape**

**Entry point & routing:** `src/legacy-pages/Admin.tsx` (line 62–83)
- Layout: `h-svh flex overflow-hidden` → left-fixed sidebar, right flex-1 column
- Routing: state-driven `section` (AdminSection union type) controlling which lazy-loaded tab renders
- **No breadcrumb,** no page title pattern; tabs are silent navigation

**Layout structure:**
- Header: `AppHeader` (shared, 56px) with theme/profile dropdown
- Main: `px-6 sm:px-8 lg:px-10 py-8` spacing, full-width flex-1 overflow-y-auto
- Sidebar: 224px (`w-56`) left gutter, `border-r border-border bg-card`

**Sidebar nav pattern** (`src/components/admin/AdminSidebar.tsx`, lines 54–88):
- Grouped sections (Overview, Users & Billing, Configuration, System) with uppercase section headers (`text-[11px]` `uppercase tracking-wider`)
- Items: `rounded-md px-3 py-2 text-sm` buttons
- Active: `bg-primary/10 text-primary`
- Hover: `hover:bg-accent hover:text-accent-foreground`
- Dividers: `my-2 h-px bg-border` between groups

**Typography & spacing in tabs:**
- Headers: `text-xl font-semibold` (DashboardTab, line 120)
- Card titles: `text-sm font-medium text-muted-foreground` (CardTitle in DashboardTab)
- Metadata: `text-xs text-muted-foreground`
- Grid gaps: `gap-4` (cards), `gap-2` (rows)
- Card padding: `CardHeader pb-2`, `CardContent` default

**Design primitives:**
- Cards: `<Card>` with `border-border` (no color tint, monochrome)
- Stat cards: `lg:grid-cols-4 gap-4` responsive grid; shadow-sm hover:shadow-md
- Tables: shadcn Table (dense, `text-sm`)
- Buttons: `variant="outline" size="sm"` for secondary; `variant="default"` for primary
- Badges: `variant="outline"` (secondary), `variant="secondary"`, `variant="success"` (green), `variant="destructive"` (red)

**Admin tabs inventory** (12 total):
- `DashboardTab` — stats grid (8 cards), 4 Recharts (Area/Bar/Line), email banner, date-range picker
- `UsersTab` — searchable/filtered table, inline edit dialog, activity drawer (Tabs: Jobs/Resumes/Usage/Payments), ban/GDPR
- `BillingTab` — nested Tabs: Plans, Payments, Subscriptions
- `PlatformSettingsTab` — nested Tabs: Config, Feature Flags
- `EmailSettingsTab` — Resend health banner, ToggleRow primitives, webhook copy, domain verification
- `AIPromptsTab` — form to edit system prompts
- `IntegrationsTab` — integration cards
- `UsageLogsTab` — table of usage events
- `AuditLogsTab` — table of audit actions
- `SystemErrorLogsTab` — error log viewer
- `SeoTab` — nested Tabs for SEO sub-sections
- `ChangelogTab` — changelog editor

**Current visual character** (5–8 sentences):
The admin panel is a side-navigation interface with minimal visual hierarchy. It uses monochrome neutral colors, thin borders, and compact density overall. Cards are understated (shadow-sm) with no background color variations—all cards render with the same card-background. Section headers within tabs are left-aligned plain text. Stats are displayed as 4-column grids of equal cards. Tables use compact row heights with icon buttons for actions. There is no breadcrumb or page title at the top of each tab—just the floating section header ("Dashboard Overview"). The overall aesthetic is utilitarian and data-focused, leaning toward "admin tooling" rather than integrated product.

---

### **2. Live App Design Language (The Target)**

**Key pages & patterns:**
- `src/legacy-pages/Index.tsx` (dashboard): hero section, stats grid, recent jobs list, onboarding card
- `src/legacy-pages/Settings.tsx`: icon + CardTitle + Switch pattern, three Card sections
- `src/legacy-pages/Billing.tsx`: feature grid, plan cards, feature comparison table
- `src/components/AppHeader.tsx`: breadcrumb (text-xs), theme toggle 3-button group, profile initials button (h-9 w-9 bg-primary text-primary-foreground)
- `src/components/JobSidebar.tsx`: collapsible sidebar with section labels, text-[13px] nav items, icon + label rhythm
- `src/components/SidebarLayout.tsx`: outer SidebarProvider + JobSidebar, inner rounded-xl border wrapper

**Live app card & typography tokens actually used:**
- Main content padding: `px-6 sm:px-8 lg:px-10 py-8` (matched to admin)
- Card styling: `border border-border/60 shadow-sm` (thin gray border + subtle shadow, *not* monochrome)
- Card bg: `bg-card` (white/light neutral) with no overlay color
- Stat cards: icon in small badge (`h-11 w-11 rounded-xl bg-[color]/10 text-[color]`), label `text-xs text-muted-foreground`, value `text-2xl font-bold`
- Section headers: `h2 className="text-sm font-semibold text-foreground"` (Recent Jobs, Getting Started)
- Description text: `text-sm text-muted-foreground`
- Buttons: `<Button className="gap-2">` with icon + label (Plus icon + "Create Job")
- Badges: `variant="success"` (emerald), `variant="warning"` (amber), `variant="outline"`
- Tables: `<Table>` with `<TableHead>` (text-sm), `<TableBody>` rows (text-sm), icons are inline (Briefcase h-4 w-4)
- Job item row: icon badge (`h-9 w-9 rounded-lg bg-primary/10`), title (text-sm), metadata (text-xs muted)
- Icon sizes: 4x4 (inline), 5x5 (titles), 6x6 (large stat icons)

**Typography scale actually used:**
- text-[10.5px] (sidebar section labels)
- text-xs (13px equivalent: metadata, badge labels, secondary)
- text-[13px] (nav items in sidebar)
- text-sm (14px: table cells, descriptions, secondary headings)
- text-base (16px: form labels, body)
- text-2xl (24px: stat values)
- font-bold (stat values, hero name)
- font-semibold (h2, card titles)
- font-medium (button text, nav active)

**Color & spacing rhythm:**
- Sidebar: `bg-sidebar` (light gray/white), nav items `text-muted-foreground`, active `bg-sidebar-accent text-sidebar-accent-foreground`
- Icons: always paired with label, color = `text-primary` or inherited
- Spacing: consistent `gap-2`, `gap-3`, `gap-4` grid/flex rhythm
- Borders: thin 1px `border-border` (light gray), hover adds shadow not bg color
- Empty states: centered text-muted-foreground (no styled containers)
- Badges: colored variant (emerald for success, amber for pending, red for error)

**3–5 DEFINING design choices:**
1. **Card borders are thin 1px borders + subtle shadow, not background fills** — every card uses `border border-border/60 shadow-sm`, never background colors for hierarchy
2. **Typography is compact & dense: text-xs/text-sm dominates**, sidebar nav is text-[13px], metadata is text-xs — creates "product density" not "admin sparseness"
3. **Icons are always paired with text labels in a consistent icon-label rhythm** (gap-2.5 or gap-3), never icon-only except in action buttons
4. **Color is used sparingly for status badges only** (emerald/amber/red), rest is monochrome text-muted-foreground/text-foreground
5. **Sidebar is collapsible + persistent, not hidden** — main nav is always left, not top or floating; state cookie-persisted

---

### **3. Gap Analysis**

**Key deviations (admin vs. live app):**

1. **Admin sidebar is separate layout, not integrated** — Admin.tsx has own `AdminSidebar` component (224px hardcoded), not using the collapsible `JobSidebar` + `SidebarLayout` + `SidebarProvider` that all other pages use. Creates two separate navigation paradigms.

2. **Admin has NO breadcrumb or page title** — live app every page has breadcrumb + section header in AppHeader (Index.tsx shows "Dashboard" in BreadcrumbPage). Admin tabs render silent (no "Admin > Users" indicator).

3. **Admin card density is lower, spacing is looser** — compare DashboardTab stat grid (`lg:grid-cols-4 gap-4`) vs Index.tsx stat grid (`sm:grid-cols-4 gap-4`). Admin has more whitespace. Live app cards are more compact.

4. **Admin stats cards have different visual weight** — DashboardTab cards use `text-2xl font-bold` for value (same as live), but CardTitle is `text-sm font-medium text-muted-foreground` *without* icon badge. Live app stats have icon badge (`h-11 w-11 rounded-xl bg-[color]/10`), which gives visual anchoring.

5. **Admin buttons are smaller / fewer CTAs** — admin tabs rarely have hero buttons (just internal buttons). Live app every section has one clear CTA (Create Job button, hero-sized at top).

6. **Admin table styling is generic shadcn, not customized** — UsersTab uses default `<Table>`, no row hover states, no colored status badges inline like live app JobsOverviewCard shows.

7. **Admin GroupIcons in sidebar are "decorative", not functional** — AdminSidebar renders a GroupIcon per section group (Eye, UserCog, Wrench, Server icons) in header, but these don't open/collapse the group. Adds noise.

8. **Admin section headers are inconsistent** — some tabs say "Dashboard Overview" (h2 text-xl), some say "User Management" (CardTitle text-lg), some have no header (Settings sub-tabs). Live app always uses `<h1>` or `<h2>` with consistent sizing.

9. **Admin has no onboarding/empty state messaging** — UsersTab shows "No users found" as plain text, not a Card with icon + explanation. Live app has "Getting Started" card with numbered steps.

10. **Admin dates/times are raw `.toLocaleDateString()`** — no fuzzy relative time (e.g., "2 days ago"), just "4/14/2026". Live app format is more human.

**5–7 most impactful changes to align:**
1. **Use `SidebarLayout` + `JobSidebar` instead of custom `AdminSidebar`** — integrate admin into collapsible persistent sidebar, use same nav structure as all authenticated pages
2. **Add breadcrumb + page title to admin tabs** — each tab gets "Admin > [Tab Name]" breadcrumb + h1/h2 page title above content (see AppHeader pattern)
3. **Add stat card icon badges** — admin stat cards should use `h-11 w-11 rounded-xl bg-[color]/10` icon containers, match live app visual weight
4. **Tighten card grid gaps & padding** — reduce `gap-4` to `gap-3`, reduce vertical py padding to match live app density
5. **Add inline status badges to tables** — admin tables should use colored Badge variants (success/warning/destructive) for status, not muted text
6. **Remove GroupIcon headers from sidebar** — simplify section labels to just text (no icons), reduce visual noise
7. **Adopt single admin nav pattern** — deprecate AdminSection routing; make admin tabs URL-routable (e.g., `/admin/users`, `/admin/billing`) using Next params, not state

The admin panel is a side-navigation interface with minimal visual hierarchy. It uses monochrome neutral colors, thin borders, and compact density overall. ### **2. Live App Design Language (The Target)**

**Key pages & patterns:**
- `src/legacy-pages/Index.tsx` (dashboard): hero section, stats grid, recent jobs list, onboarding card
- `src/legacy-pages/Settings.tsx`: icon + CardTitle + Switch pattern, three Card sections
- `src/legacy-pages/Billing.tsx`: feature grid, plan cards, feature comparison table
- `src/components/AppHeader.tsx`: breadcrumb (text-xs), theme toggle 3-button group, profile initials button (h-9 w-9 bg-primary text-primary-foreground)

- `src/components/SidebarLayout.tsx`: outer SidebarProvider + JobSidebar, inner rounded-xl border wrapper

**Live app card & typography tokens actually used:**
- Main content padding: `px-6 sm:px-8 lg:px-10 py-8` (matched to admin)
- Card styling: `border border-border/60 shadow-sm` (thin gray border + subtle shadow, *not* monochrome)
- Card bg: `bg-card` (white/light neutral) with no overlay color
- Stat cards: icon in small badge (`h-11 w-11 rounded-xl bg-[color]/10 text-[color]`), label `text-xs text-muted-foreground`, value `text-2xl font-bold`
- Section headers: `h2 className="text-sm font-semibold text-foreground"` (Recent Jobs, Getting Started)
- Description text: `text-sm text-muted-foreground`
- Buttons: `<Button className="gap-2">` with icon + label (Plus icon + "Create Job")
- Badges: `variant="success"` (emerald), `variant="warning"` (amber), `variant="outline"`
- Tables: `<Table>` with `<TableHead>` (text-sm), `<TableBody>` rows (text-sm), icons are inline (Briefcase h-4 w-4)
- Job item row: icon badge (`h-9 w-9 rounded-lg bg-primary/10`), title (text-sm), metadata (text-xs muted)
- Icon sizes: 4x4 (inline), 5x5 (titles), 6x6 (large stat icons)

**Typography scale actually used:**
- text-[10.5px] (sidebar section labels)
- text-xs (13px equivalent: metadata, badge labels, secondary)
- text-[13px] (nav items in sidebar)
- text-sm (14px: table cells, descriptions, secondary headings)
- text-base (16px: form labels, body)
- text-2xl (24px: stat values)
- font-bold (stat values, hero name)
- font-semibold (h2, card titles)
- font-medium (button text, nav active)

**Color & spacing rhythm:**
- Sidebar: `bg-sidebar` (light gray/white), nav items `text-muted-foreground`, active `bg-sidebar-accent text-sidebar-accent-foreground`
- Icons: always paired with label, color = `text-primary` or inherited
- Spacing: consistent `gap-2`, `gap-3`, `gap-4` grid/flex rhythm
- Borders: thin 1px `border-border` (light gray), hover adds shadow not bg color
- Empty states: centered text-muted-foreground (no styled containers)
- Badges: colored variant (emerald for success, amber for pending, red for error)

**3–5 DEFINING design choices:**
1. **Card borders are thin 1px borders + subtle shadow, not background fills** — every card uses `border border-border/60 shadow-sm`, never background colors for hierarchy
2. **Typography is compact & dense: text-xs/text-sm dominates**, sidebar nav is text-[13px], metadata is text-xs — creates "product density" not "admin sparseness"
3. **Icons are always paired with text labels in a consistent icon-label rhythm** (gap-2.5 or gap-3), never icon-only except in action buttons
4. **Color is used sparingly for status badges only** (emerald/amber/red), rest is monochrome text-muted-foreground/text-foreground
5. **Sidebar is collapsible + persistent, not hidden** — main nav is always left, not top or floating; state cookie-persisted

---

### **3. Gap Analysis**

**Key deviations (admin vs. live app):**

1. **Admin sidebar is separate layout, not integrated** — Admin.tsx has own `AdminSidebar` component (224px hardcoded), not using the collapsible `JobSidebar` + `SidebarLayout` + `SidebarProvider` that all other pages use. Creates two separate navigation paradigms.

2. **Admin has NO breadcrumb or page title** — live app every page has breadcrumb + section header in AppHeader (Index.tsx shows "Dashboard" in BreadcrumbPage). Admin tabs render silent (no "Admin > Users" indicator).

3. **Admin card density is lower, spacing is looser** — compare DashboardTab stat grid (`lg:grid-cols-4 gap-4`) vs Index.tsx stat grid (`sm:grid-cols-4 gap-4`). Admin has more whitespace. Live app cards are more compact.

4. **Admin stats cards have different visual weight** — DashboardTab cards use `text-2xl font-bold` for value (same as live), but CardTitle is `text-sm font-medium text-muted-foreground` *without* icon badge. Live app stats have icon badge (`h-11 w-11 rounded-xl bg-[color]/10`), which gives visual anchoring.

5. **Admin buttons are smaller / fewer CTAs** — admin tabs rarely have hero buttons (just internal buttons). Live app every section has one clear CTA (Create Job button, hero-sized at top).

6. **Admin table styling is generic shadcn, not customized** — UsersTab uses default `<Table>`, no row hover states, no colored status badges inline like live app JobsOverviewCard shows.

7. **Admin GroupIcons in sidebar are "decorative", not functional** — AdminSidebar renders a GroupIcon per section group (Eye, UserCog, Wrench, Server icons) in header, but these don't open/collapse the group. Adds noise.

8. **Admin section headers are inconsistent** — some tabs say "Dashboard Overview" (h2 text-xl), some say "User Management" (CardTitle text-lg), some have no header (Settings sub-tabs). Live app always uses `<h1>` or `<h2>` with consistent sizing.

9. **Admin has no onboarding/empty state messaging** — UsersTab shows "No users found" as plain text, not a Card with icon + explanation. Live app has "Getting Started" card with numbered steps.

10. **Admin dates/times are raw `.toLocaleDateString()`** — no fuzzy relative time (e.g., "2 days ago"), just "4/14/2026". Live app format is more human.

**5–7 most impactful changes to align:**
1. **Use `SidebarLayout` + `JobSidebar` instead of custom `AdminSidebar`** — integrate admin into collapsible persistent sidebar, use same nav structure as all authenticated pages
2. **Add breadcrumb + page title to admin tabs** — each tab gets "Admin > [Tab Name]" breadcrumb + h1/h2 page title above content (see AppHeader pattern)
3. **Add stat card icon badges** — admin stat cards should use `h-11 w-11 rounded-xl bg-[color]/10` icon containers, match live app visual weight
4. **Tighten card grid gaps & padding** — reduce `gap-4` to `gap-3`, reduce vertical py padding to match live app density
5. **Add inline status badges to tables** — admin tables should use colored Badge variants (success/warning/destructive) for status, not muted text
6. **Remove GroupIcon headers from sidebar** — simplify section labels to just text (no icons), reduce visual noise
7. **Adopt single admin nav pattern** — deprecate AdminSection routing; make admin tabs URL-routable (e.g., `/admin/users`, `/admin/billing`) using Next params, not state

content.thinking:
Looking at the pricing comparison HTML, I can see it outlines four subscription tiers—Free, Starter, Growth, and what appears to be an Enterprise plan that got cut off—each with different job limits, CV allocations, and member access levels. I need to check how these compare against what's currently implemented in the Billing component.

The main gaps I'm noticing: the app is displaying USD pricing when the HTML clearly uses INR, the plan feature cards don't show the specific limits (jobs, CVs, team members) that are visible in the comparison, and there's no incremental "what you gain" messaging between tiers. I should verify whether the Supabase plans table actually has these four plans seeded with the correct INR pricing and feature limits. Looking at the database schema, the `limits_json` column probably stores some limits like AI credits, but it's missing explicit fields for active jobs, CVs per month, and team members — the key differentiators between plans. The plan cards in the app only display price and generic features, whereas the comparison HTML shows specific limits and audience positioning for each tier. I also notice the billing page lacks currency flexibility (showing `$0` when the reference uses INR) and doesn't include the "adds over previous plan" feature lists or the audience labels like "Solo recruiter" and "Small team" that appear in the HTML version. I'm noticing the database schema is missing several key columns that would support the pricing page features — things like active job limits, CV monthly quotas, team member caps, and audience labels that should be tied to each plan. The pricing structure also needs to handle annual savings calculations and multi-currency support, while the business logic is missing upgrade previews with prorated costs, usage warnings when customers approach their limits, invoice downloads, and tax handling for different regions. Let me quickly verify what's actually in the PLAN_FEATURES and whether all four plans exist in the database.

# Plan: Rankora Positioning + Billing Rebuild (Truth-Telling Edition)

## Context

The comparison HTML the user dropped in is half-aspirational — it claims
WhatsApp, custom domain, AI rejection emails, and other features that
don't exist in the codebase. We just audited the actual feature surface
(see "Real feature inventory" below) and it tells a much more focused
story than the comparison sheet implies.

User decisions that shape this plan:

- **Geography:** Multi-region from day one (₹ / $ / £ / € with geo-detect).
- **Primary customer:** In-house recruiting teams at startups and SMBs.
  Agency tooling stays available but is no longer the marketing wedge.

The job is to (1) pick a defensible positioning that matches what
Rankora actually ships, (2) rebuild the billing page so it sells the
real product instead of an imagined one, and (3) define the next-build
list to close the gaps that matter.

---

## 1. Recommended positioning

> **"The AI-first ATS that catches AI-written resumes — at flat per-team
> pricing, not per-seat."**

Tool category: **AI-native applicant tracking system for in-house
recruiting teams (5-50 hires/year)**. Closest peers: Skima AI, Manatal
Pro. We are NOT trying to be hireEZ (passive sourcing) or Recruiterflow
(agency CRM) — those need integration breadth and per-user revenue
models we don't have and shouldn't chase yet.

**Five wedges — every one backed by code that already exists:**

1. **Deep AI scoring** — multi-dimensional (skills, experience, tools,
   education, must-haves), embeddings-based, GPT-4o, with heuristic
   fallback. Not a keyword match. ([rank-resumes/index.ts])
2. **AI Authenticity Check** — detects AI-generated resumes. Genuinely
   unique in the market right now.
   ([check-authenticity/index.ts], [AuthenticityBadge.tsx])
3. **AI Interview Question generation** — tailored per candidate, ships
   from the Free tier. ([InterviewQuestionsPanel.tsx])
4. **Email sequences with multi-step delays** — multi-channel (email +
   SMS), enrollment-based. Currently undermarketed.
   ([sequences table], [send-sequence-step/index.ts])
5. **Flat per-team pricing** — beats every per-seat competitor for any
   team of 3+. Manatal Enterprise = $35/user/mo; Recruiterflow Pro =
   $119/user/mo. We charge one flat fee per workspace.

**Hidden upsell:** Agency mode (clients, mandates, placements,
commissions, invoices) is fully built and ships in the Agency tier.
We position it as "also great for boutique recruiting agencies"
without making it the headline.

---

## 2. Real feature inventory (built vs claimed)

### ✅ Built and shipping
- AI scoring engine (rank-resumes, analyze-jd, parse-resume)
- AI JD generator, AI summary cards, AI interview questions
- AI authenticity check, AI semantic search, JD rewriter
- ATS core: jobs, resumes, pipeline stages, candidate notes/tags,
  scorecards, custom forms with knockout questions, CSV import/export
- Email sequences (multi-step, delay-based), SMS via Twilio
- Branded career pages with Google Jobs JSON-LD + Indeed XML feed
- Interview booking with timezone-aware availability slots
- Talent pool with rediscovery (semantic search of past candidates)
- Agency hub (clients, mandates, placements, commissions, invoices)
- Stage automations, activity feed, audit logs (admin)
- Public REST API + API key management, Chrome extension (basic)
- Team invites + roles, GDPR data export, FAQ/AEO SEO

### ⚠️ Claimed in marketing/comparison docs but NOT built — drop these
- **WhatsApp messaging** — UI placeholder only, no Twilio WhatsApp
  integration. **Stop claiming this.**
- **Custom domain for career page** — only Rankora subdomain works.
- **LinkedIn auto-posting / job board distribution** — share links only.
- **SSO (SAML/OIDC)** — UI text only, no provider integration.
- **Bias-blind mode** — schema exists, scoring logic doesn't honour it.
- **2,500+ integrations** — we have ~10. Stop the number game.
- **Webhook dispatcher** — table exists, nothing fires events. P1 fix.
- **AI rejection email drafting** — claimed in current Billing.tsx,
  not implemented anywhere. P1 fix.
- **Zapier app** — not built. Need public API + webhooks first.

### 💎 Built but undermarketed — promote these
- **Stage automations** (StageAutomationManager.tsx) — auto-advance
  candidates on criteria match. Buried in admin.
- **Talent pool rediscovery** — semantic search resurfaces past
  candidates for new jobs. Not in main nav.
- **Interview booking with timezone availability** — full self-serve
  scheduling. Currently invisible in marketing.
- **Public REST API with full CRUD** — already shipping.
- **Chrome extension for sourcing** — built, no marketplace listing.
- **Activity heatmap analytics** — buried in Reports.

---

## 3. Pricing strategy

**Model:** Flat per-team per-month, with annual discount (~20%).
4 plans, multi-currency from day one, geo-detected on first paint.

| Plan    | Audience              | Active Jobs | CVs/mo | Members | Monthly (₹/$/£/€)        | Annual (₹/$/£/€)         |
|---------|-----------------------|-------------|--------|---------|--------------------------|--------------------------|
| Free    | Solo recruiter        | 1           | 50     | 1       | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0           | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0           |
| Starter | Small in-house team   | 5           | 500    | ∞       | 3,799 / 49 / 39 / 45     | 2,999 / 39 / 31 / 36     |
| Growth ⭐| Mid-size in-house     | 20          | 2,000  | ∞       | 8,799 / 109 / 89 / 99    | 6,999 / 89 / 71 / 82     |
| Agency  | Large in-house OR agency | ∞        | 10,000 | ∞       | 16,499 / 209 / 169 / 189 | 12,999 / 169 / 135 / 155 |

(Conversion is approximate — final numbers are a product call. Annual
column is the per-month price when billed yearly.)

**Why flat-per-team beats per-seat:**
A 5-person in-house team using Recruiterflow Pro pays $595/mo. Same
team on Rankora Growth pays $89/mo flat. That delta is the entire
acquisition pitch.

**India-specific:** GST (18%) shown as a line item, not embedded.
Indian customers see "+ 18% GST" disclosure under each price.

---

## 4. Build list (gap-closure, prioritized)

### Sprint 1 — Truth-telling (this work)

**Migration `20260420000022_pricing_redesign.sql`:**
- Wipe + reseed `plans` with 4 plans × 2 billing intervals × 4 currencies = 32 rows (or 4 plans × 2 intervals with `prices_json {INR, USD, GBP, EUR}` — single column is cleaner).
- Add columns: `audience_label text`, `is_popular boolean`,
  `feature_highlights jsonb`, `limits_json` updated to include
  `active_jobs`, `cvs_per_month`, `team_members`, `talent_pool` (-1 = ∞).
- Drop the obsolete `pro` plan row (replaced by Starter/Growth).

**`src/lib/currency.ts` (new):**
- `detectCurrency()` — geo-detect from `Accept-Language` + `navigator.language`; fallback to USD; cache in localStorage.
- `formatPrice(amountMinor, currency)` — `Intl.NumberFormat` per locale.
- `currencySymbol(currency)` and `currencyOptions = [INR, USD, GBP, EUR]`.

**`src/legacy-pages/Billing.tsx` rebuild:**
- Strip the bottom-table comparison rows that don't match real features:
  drop **WhatsApp Messaging**, **Custom Domain**, **AI Rejection Emails**
  (or mark "Q1 2026"), **LinkedIn enrichment** (never claimed but worth
  not adding back).
- New plan cards (extract to `src/components/billing/PlanCard.tsx`)
  showing: audience badge, currency-aware price, "billed annually"
  subtext + actual computed savings %, **explicit limit grid** (Jobs /
  CVs / Members / Talent Pool), per-plan **"Adds over [previous tier]"**
  feature list pulled from `feature_highlights` jsonb.
- Currency switcher in the header (₹ / $ / £ / €), persists per user.
- **Why Rankora strip** (`src/components/billing/WhyRankora.tsx`) above
  the table: 3 differentiators (AI Authenticity, Flat Pricing, Sequences)
  with one-line proof each.
- **FAQ section** (`src/components/billing/PricingFAQ.tsx`): 8 questions
  (refund policy, GST handling, plan switching, credit rollover, cancel
  policy, custom plans, India billing, data ownership).
- GST disclosure block visible when currency = INR.
- Trust signals: "No credit card required for Free • Cancel anytime •
  14-day money-back on first paid month".

### Sprint 2 — Close the most damaging gaps (next pass)

1. **Webhook dispatcher** — fire events on candidate stage change, new
   application, hire outcome. Schema exists in `webhook_configs`.
2. **AI Rejection Email drafting** — new edge function `draft-rejection`
   reusing the analyze-jd context to generate personal, kind emails.
3. **Google Calendar two-way sync** — top global ask; OAuth + push slots.
4. **Slack notifications** — channel-level pings on new candidate, stage
   change, scorecard submission.

### Sprint 3 — Scale-up moves (later)

5. SSO (SAML/OIDC) — gates Enterprise tier above Agency.
6. Custom domain for career page (CNAME + SSL via proxy).
7. LinkedIn enrichment (Apollo or Clearbit API) — paid integration.
8. Greenhouse / Lever import wizard.
9. Zapier app (now possible: public API + webhooks both work).

---

## 5. What NOT to do

- **Don't try to be Manatal.** They have 2,500 integrations and 12 years
  of partnerships. We will lose that race for 3 years. Skip.
- **Don't try to be hireEZ.** Their 800M-profile passive database needs
  $50M+ in data infra. Not the play.
- **Don't add per-user pricing.** Flat-per-team is the wedge. Killing it
  to chase mid-market enterprise revenue trades the only acquisition
  story we have for a feature parity slog.
- **Don't ship more agency-specific marketing.** The features stay; the
  positioning becomes secondary. In-house first.
- **Don't claim WhatsApp until WhatsApp ships.** Period.

---

## 6. Files to be modified / created

**New:**
- `supabase/migrations/20260420000022_pricing_redesign.sql`
- `src/lib/currency.ts`
- `src/components/billing/PlanCard.tsx`
- `src/components/billing/WhyRankora.tsx`
- `src/components/billing/PricingFAQ.tsx`
- `src/components/billing/CurrencySwitcher.tsx`

**Modified:**
- `src/legacy-pages/Billing.tsx` — full rebuild around new components
- `src/components/admin/PlansTab.tsx` — surface new columns (audience_label, is_popular, feature_highlights, multi-currency prices)

**Reuses (do not duplicate):**
- Existing `FEATURE_COMPARISON` table data in [Billing.tsx:43-129] — keep, just trim the rows we don't actually ship
- Existing `handleSubscribe` / `handleCancelSubscription` / `handleDowngradeToFree` flows in [Billing.tsx:196-265]
- `useAuth` profile fetch for current plan resolution
- `create-dodo-checkout` edge function — already multi-currency capable via Dodo

---

## 7. Verification

Before shipping Sprint 1:

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors.
2. `npx vitest run` — 246 passing.
3. `npx next build` — clean.
4. `npx supabase db push` — migration applies clean on develop.
5. Manual: load `/billing`, switch each currency, confirm:
   - 4 plan cards render with correct prices in each currency
   - Annual savings % is computed (not hardcoded)
   - Limits grid shows Jobs/CVs/Members/Talent Pool per plan
   - GST disclosure appears only when INR is selected
   - "Adds over [previous]" feature lists are correct per plan
   - Comparison table at the bottom does not contain WhatsApp,
     Custom Domain, or AI Rejection Emails rows
   - Subscribe flow still hits `create-dodo-checkout` and redirects
6. Manual: open `/admin` → Billing → Plans. Verify all 8 plan rows
   (4 plans × 2 intervals) are present and editable.

---

## 8. Open question for after Sprint 1

Once the truthful billing page is live, we'll know which of Sprint 2's
four gaps customers ask for most. Default order is Webhook Dispatcher →
AI Rejection Emails → Google Calendar → Slack, but that's reorderable
based on first-week support tickets.

models we don't have and shouldn't chase yet.

**Five wedges — every one backed by code that already exists:**

1. **Deep AI scoring** — multi-dimensional (skills, experience, tools,
   education, must-haves), embeddings-based, GPT-4o, with heuristic
   fallback. Not a keyword match. ([rank-resumes/index.ts])
2. **AI Authenticity Check** — detects AI-generated resumes. Genuinely
   unique in the market right now.
   ([check-authenticity/index.ts], [AuthenticityBadge.tsx])
3. **AI Interview Question generation** — tailored per candidate, ships
   from the Free tier. ([InterviewQuestionsPanel.tsx])
4. **Email sequences with multi-step delays** — multi-channel (email +
   SMS), enrollment-based. Currently undermarketed.
   ([sequences table], [send-sequence-step/index.ts])
5. **Flat per-team pricing** — beats every per-seat competitor for any
   team of 3+. Manatal Enterprise = $35/user/mo; Recruiterflow Pro =
   $119/user/mo. We charge one flat fee per workspace.

commissions, invoices) is fully built and ships in the Agency tier.

without making it the headline.

## 3. Pricing strategy

**Model:** Flat per-team per-month, with annual discount (~20%).
4 plans, multi-currency from day one, geo-detected on first paint.

| Plan    | Audience              | Active Jobs | CVs/mo | Members | Monthly (₹/$/£/€)        | Annual (₹/$/£/€)         |
|---------|-----------------------|-------------|--------|---------|--------------------------|--------------------------|
| Free    | Solo recruiter        | 1           | 50     | 1       | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0           | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0           |
| Starter | Small in-house team   | 5           | 500    | ∞       | 3,799 / 49 / 39 / 45     | 2,999 / 39 / 31 / 36     |
| Growth ⭐| Mid-size in-house     | 20          | 2,000  | ∞       | 8,799 / 109 / 89 / 99    | 6,999 / 89 / 71 / 82     |
| Agency  | Large in-house OR agency | ∞        | 10,000 | ∞       | 16,499 / 209 / 169 / 189 | 12,999 / 169 / 135 / 155 |

(Conversion is approximate — final numbers are a product call. Annual
column is the per-month price when billed yearly.)

**Why flat-per-team beats per-seat:**
A 5-person in-house team using Recruiterflow Pro pays $595/mo. Same
team on Rankora Growth pays $89/mo flat. That delta is the entire
acquisition pitch.

**India-specific:** GST (18%) shown as a line item, not embedded.
Indian customers see "+ 18% GST" disclosure under each price.
